concepts.name: Argus Live — the Decision Room (a standing, replayable reasoning session, not an export)
concepts.one_line: Argus stops being a document factory and becomes a persistent, addressable, replayable Decision Room: every voyage is a living URL you reopen, re-run, fork, and watch decay — the deliverable is the session itself, kept alive, never "exported."
concepts.thesis: The current shape's local maximum is the "export." Argus spends 2670 lines of ProgressiveFlow + a context chain + working eval engines to manufacture four markdown files — and the instant they're produced, the product's relationship to the user ends. Blindspot proved this: outputs are orphaned static markdown, the learning loop is one-way, and retention is empirically unvalidated. C's answer is to bolt a reflection TAB ("Mirror / Sense of the Route") onto the side of that same pipeline — it makes the ledger prettier but the artifact is still dead the moment it's made, and the user's reason to return is still "go read a dashboard about yourself." The radical bet: a decision is not an event that produces a document, it is a STATE that persists and degrades. The real reason a non-developer returns is not to admire a chart of their judgment — it is because a decision they made is still pending in reality, its assumptions are aging, the world moved, and the AI they were about to "recast" to has new capabilities. If the session is a living object with a URL, a heartbeat (assumption freshness), and a re-run button wired to the same llm.ts + Phase 1/2 engines, then "revisit" stops being a willpower act and becomes a notification: "3 of the assumptions behind your 'India market entry' decision are now 47 days old; one was contradicted by the outcome you logged. Re-rehearse?" The process becomes the product because the process never ends — it just goes quiet until reality pokes it.
concepts.what_fundamentally_changes: Today Argus IS a single-shot decision harness that emits 4 documents and forgets you. It becomes a registry of standing decisions, each one a live, addressable reasoning session (/room/[id]) that you reopen mid-flight, where the four "outputs" are not files but VIEWS of the session's current state — regenerated on demand, always reflecting the latest assumptions. The unit of value shifts from "the document I produced" to "the decision I'm still responsible for." A voyage doesn't "complete at 이타카" — it goes into a STANDING state with a freshness heartbeat. Re-running is first-class, not backtracking: editing the real_question forks the room (cheap, versioned) instead of triggering a feared 30s full re-analysis (the P2 blindspot finding). The retention thesis flips from pull (user must remember to come admire their Mirror) to push (the room itself decays and pings you). And critically it closes the one-way loop the deep-plan flagged: because the room is alive, the outcome you log months later flows BACK into the room's own assumptions, marking them validated/contradicted in place — the same surface, not a separate accuracy store nobody opens.
what_it_kills: The 'export' mental model entirely — FinalCard.tsx's 'Copy Document' / 'download 4 markdown files' as the terminal act. Outputs are no longer files you take away; they are live render-on-demand views (lib/export.ts, agent-spec.ts, checklist.ts become VIEW SERIALIZERS of room state, invoked each visit, never the endpoint).

이타카/voyage-completion as a terminal state — the 'you have arrived, here is your document' moment. Replaced by a STANDING state with a heartbeat. The nautical 'arrival' metaphor dies; a decision is never 'arrived,' it's pending-in-reality.

The withLog checkbox + 'decision log as optional footnote' (FinalCard.tsx:76-83, the P1 blindspot finding) — the log isn't an optional appendix to a document, it's literally the spine of the room; there is nothing else to be a footnote to.

C's standalone 'Mirror / Sense of the Route' reflection TAB as a separate retention surface — folded INTO the room. You don't visit a dashboard about your judgment; your judgment history lives as the version graph of your actual standing decisions. The across-voyages ledger is emergent, not a built screen.
The fear-gated backtracking modal C/blindspot wanted to add ('this will re-analyze, est 30s') — re-running becomes the primary verb, versioned and cheap-feeling, so the warning is obsolete.

The dual-mode legacy 4-step flow (ReframeStep/RecastStep et al. as separate ?step= entry points) — a room has no 'steps you tab between,' it has a current state and a history; legacy mode has no place to live and gets deleted.
what_it_salvages: src/lib/llm.ts (~789 lines, backoff + circuit breaker + multi-fallback JSON) — UNTOUCHED and now MORE valuable: every room re-run, fork, and freshness-triggered re-rehearse hits it, so the robust engine finally earns its complexity instead of firing once per voyage.

Phase 1 adaptive decompose + Phase 2 multi-lens recast + the working eval engines — become the room's 'recompute' core. The exact same intelligence, but invoked repeatedly against an evolving state rather than once.

context-chain.ts (typed ReframeContext/RecastContext + mergeAssumptionsIntoKeyAssumptions with inheritance/provenance, verified real per deep-plan self-critique) — this IS the room's data model. The radical shape just demands it be PERSISTED with _source provenance and a per-assumption timestamp + status field (validated/contradicted/stale), which is exactly the Phase 0 work the deep-plan already sequenced as foundational. We're not inventing a new spine; we're giving the existing one a heartbeat.

Supabase + the localStorage-first/sync architecture (CLAUDE.md) — already built for persistence; rooms are just ProgressiveSession rows promoted to first-class addressable entities with a status + freshness column.
useAccuracyStore / outcome-rating plumbing C identified — reused as the WRITE-BACK channel: a logged outcome stamps the specific room assumption it validates/contradicts, in place.

The Claude Code skills + plugin (reframe/recast/rehearse/blindspot) — become room ACTIONS triggerable from CLI against a room id, making the standing-decision usable from where developers/power-users actually work.
concepts.why_better_for_the_real_user: The non-developer strategist's honest problem isn't 'I need a nicely formatted strategy doc' (ChatGPT does that, and C's Mirror doesn't beat ChatGPT — it just journals). Their real problem is that they made a consequential call weeks ago, the world has shifted, and they have no idea which of their original assumptions still hold or whether the decision needs revisiting before they commit budget/headcount. 'Just ask ChatGPT' is structurally incapable of this: ChatGPT has no memory of the specific decision, no timestamped assumptions, no heartbeat, no 're-run the exact same rigorous rehearsal against what changed.' Argus Live owns the ONE thing ChatGPT can't: continuity of a specific decision over time. The win for a non-dev is concrete and emotional — they reopen /room/india-entry and see in plain language 'you assumed regulatory approval by Q2; that assumption is 47 days old and you logged that it slipped — 3 downstream steps depend on it. Re-rehearse?' That is a reason to return that requires zero discipline and zero love of dashboards, because the product reaches out when reality moves the ground under a decision they're still accountable for.
concepts.biggest_risk: Decisions may not actually have a long enough 'live' tail to sustain push-retention — most casual non-dev users may make a call, ship it, and never care again, meaning the heartbeat pings into the void and feel like spam (the same empirically-unvalidated-retention trap, just relocated). Equally, 'freshness/decay' requires a credible signal that an assumption is stale — without the user logging outcomes or some external world-signal, decay is just a timer, and a timer-driven 'your assumption is 47 days old' ping is noise, not insight. The whole bet rests on assumptions being individually addressable, time-stamped, and outcome-linkable — which means the Phase 0 persisted-provenance-context-chain (the deep-plan's hardest 2-week foundation) is a HARD prerequisite, not optional; if that slips, the radical shape collapses back into 'a saved session with a re-run button.'
concepts.cheapest_proof: Don't build rooms, decay, or notifications. Run a 2-week Wizard-of-Oz on existing users: take ~15 completed voyages already in Supabase, and 3-6 weeks after completion send each user ONE manual message naming a specific original assumption from their voyage and asking 'Is this still true? Does this decision need a fresh look?' with a single 'Re-open & re-rehearse' link that just reloads their old session into the current flow. Measure two numbers only: (1) reply/click-through rate vs. a control group pinged with C's 'come see your judgment patterns' Mirror framing, and (2) of those who re-open, how many actually re-run vs. bounce. If the decision-still-pending framing beats the self-reflection framing on return AND a non-trivial fraction re-run, the living-room thesis is alive and the Phase 0 investment is justified. If nobody cares that their old assumptions aged, kill the radical shape and ship C's incremental Mirror — it's cheaper and the honest winner.

concepts.name: Argus Verdict — the harness that grades its own advice
concepts.one_line: Stop shipping four markdown files and walking away; instead embed Argus AT the Claude Code / Cursor execution boundary so the same judgment engine that planned the work watches the work happen, scores its own pre-flight calls against what actually shipped, and turns "did the flagged risk materialize?" from a question the user types into a fact Argus observes.
concepts.thesis: The current shape is a local maximum because it severs itself from the only event that can prove it was right: execution. ARGUS today is a decision harness that ends at the artifact — four orphaned markdown docs (Brief/Chain/Spec/Checklist via FinalCard + progressive-handoff) handed to a user who then leaves for Claude Code/Cursor and never comes back. Blindspot's headline ("what the code SAYS vs what PRODUCTION does") and its two P0s ("no execution instrumentation", "outputs don't drive retention") are not bugs to patch — they are the same wound: Argus has no feedback from reality, so its learning loop is structurally one-way (signal-recorder.ts collects, navigator.ts never acts) and its core promise ("think before you recast") can never be graded. C (incremental) feels this and reaches for it, but flinches: C's "did the flagged risk materialize?" is a MANUAL prompt the user types days later — self-report about a tool they already abandoned, the weakest possible signal, gated on a user who left. The radical bet: the judgment is only worth accumulating if it's CALIBRATED, and calibration is impossible without watching execution. So move Argus to where execution lives. ARGUS already ships skills (reframe/recast/rehearse/blindspot) + a plugin INTO Claude Code — the execution boundary is already half-occupied. Turn that beachhead into the product: a planning pass that emits not a doc but a live "decision contract" (the recast's AI-vs-human assignments + blindspot's flagged risks, as checkable predicates), then a thin runtime wrapper/hook that observes the actual session (which steps the agent did, which the human overrode, which flagged risk actually fired, whether the governing_idea survived contact) and posts a Verdict back. Argus stops being a doc generator beside execution and becomes the judgment layer wrapped around it — the only configuration in which "you get smarter every use" is true rather than aspirational, because every run produces a graded prediction, not a saved opinion.
concepts.what_fundamentally_changes: Today Argus IS a pre-flight document generator: a beautiful standalone web voyage whose output is inert markdown and whose competitor ("just ask ChatGPT") wins because ChatGPT also produces text and is one tab closer to execution. After this, Argus IS a closed-loop judgment instrument that lives at the execution seam: it makes falsifiable pre-flight calls ("this step must be human-judged"; "the CFO-cost risk will surface here"; "the real question is X not Y"), then measures them against what the agent runtime actually did, and reports a Verdict + calibration score. The unit of value shifts from "a document I read once" to "a prediction that got graded" — which means the retention asset (C's Logbook / navigator judgment layer) becomes a TRACK RECORD ("your risk-flags hit 71%; you over-trust the AI on data steps") instead of a mood-board of unvalidated self-reflection. The competitor flips too: you cannot get a calibrated judgment track record from ChatGPT, because ChatGPT doesn't watch your execution and doesn't remember being wrong. Argus becomes the thing that sits between intention and execution and keeps score — a harness in the literal engineering sense (a test/observation rig), not the nautical metaphor sense.
what_it_kills: The four orphaned static-markdown outputs as the TERMINAL deliverable (FinalCard.tsx export, progressive-handoff): Brief/Chain/Spec/Checklist stop being the end of the product and become the serializable 'decision contract' that the runtime wrapper later reads back and grades — markdown survives as a wire format, dies as the point of the product.

The standalone web app as the PRIMARY surface and the voyage-completion ceremony as the climax: 이타카/'arrival at the document' is no longer the end state. The web app demotes to a planning console + Verdict dashboard; the climax moves to post-execution ('here is how your plan survived contact').

C's MANUAL self-report outcome prompt ('did the flagged risk actually materialize?' typed by the user later) — killed and replaced by an OBSERVED outcome from the runtime hook. The whole point is that this signal must be measured, not remembered.
The one-way learning loop: signal-recorder.ts collecting signals that navigator.ts never consumes. Either it now feeds calibration, or it's dead weight.

The pretense of 'an AI team watches with you' (the HeroFlow team-assembly animation blindspot flagged as theatrical) — replaced by a real, smaller claim: 'Argus watches your execution and tells you where your plan was wrong.'
The nautical metaphor as load-bearing UX (reframe→recast→rehearse→refine→이타카 as the product's spine). It can stay as flavor but it cannot carry an instrument whose value is a calibration number.
what_it_salvages: src/lib/llm.ts (~789 lines: backoff + circuit breaker + multi-fallback JSON) — kept whole; the runtime wrapper's 'compare plan vs actual' and 'classify what the agent did' are LLM calls that need exactly this resilience at the execution boundary where flakiness is higher.

Phase 1 adaptive decompose + Phase 2 multi-lens recast with their working eval engines — these BECOME the contract generator: the recast's AI-vs-human role assignments and the decompose's critical_path are precisely the falsifiable predicates the wrapper checks against the real session.

The Claude Code skills (reframe/recast/rehearse/blindspot) + the existing plugin — THE wedge. They already execute inside Claude Code. They get a sibling: an observe/verdict skill (or a hook on Stop/PostToolUse) that reads the contract and the transcript. This is the cheapest possible execution-boundary foothold on this stack.

context-chain.ts / context-builder.ts (typed reframe→recast→exec handoff) — repurposed as the schema for the decision contract; the typed provenance is what makes a predicate checkable rather than prose.

navigator.ts / getUserPatterns / judgment-vitality / signal-recorder.ts (the judgment layer C wanted to promote) — kept, but upgraded from 'visible self-reflection' to 'calibrated track record' once it's fed observed outcomes.
blindspot's risk-classification engine — its flagged risks become the highest-value predicates to grade ('did this risk fire?'), which is also the most differentiated thing ChatGPT cannot do.
concepts.why_better_for_the_real_user: The real user is a NON-developer strategist deciding WHAT to have AI do, whose honest alternative is pasting the problem into ChatGPT. Against that, today's Argus loses on the merits: it's more friction (30-40s, a voyage, four docs) to produce text the user must still re-key into the actual AI tool — ChatGPT is closer to the action and also outputs text. The execution-bound shape gives the strategist the one thing ChatGPT structurally cannot: 'Last time you told the AI to handle the pricing analysis itself, you overrode it 40% of the way through and the cost-risk Argus flagged is exactly what tripped you. This time, hold that step.' That is judgment calibrated by the strategist's OWN history of being right and wrong about delegating to AI — the literal 'think before you recast' promise, finally falsifiable. ChatGPT cannot say it because ChatGPT does not watch what the strategist actually did next and does not keep score. It also fixes the non-developer's deepest fear — 'I don't know which parts of this I can trust the AI with' — with evidence instead of vibes: the AI-vs-human boundary stops being a one-time guess in a doc and becomes a position that gets graded and tuned to this person's demonstrated judgment.
concepts.biggest_risk: Distribution and observability collapse the user base. The whole bet rests on Argus being able to OBSERVE real execution — which on this stack means the agent runtime is Claude Code (skills/hooks can read the session/transcript) or Cursor. But the stated target user is a NON-developer strategist, and non-developers overwhelmingly do NOT execute in Claude Code/Cursor — they execute in ChatGPT, a chat UI, or by hand, none of which expose an instrumentable boundary Argus can hook. So there's a brutal scissors: the users who give clean execution signal (developers in agent runtimes) are not the target persona, and the target persona executes where Argus is blind. If you weaken 'observe' to 'user self-reports outcome,' you have collapsed back into C's manual prompt and the radical bet evaporates. Secondary risk: even with a hook, mapping a messy real transcript to 'did predicate P hold?' is itself an LLM judgment that can be wrong, so a miscalibrated Verdict is worse than no verdict (it teaches the user the wrong lesson with false authority). Net honest verdict: as a REPLACEMENT for C this is probably WORSE for the stated non-developer persona because of the distribution scissors; it is BETTER only if you either (a) accept a pivot of the target user toward 'people who execute with AI agents,' or (b) ship it as an additive 'Pro/dev' loop on top of C's incremental web product rather than instead of it. The execution-bound harness is the right NORTH for the loop-closing problem, but it should ride on C's chassis, not bulldoze it.
concepts.cheapest_proof: One week, no rewrite, ride the existing plugin. Build a single new Claude Code artifact: an 'argus-verdict' skill/hook pair. (1) When a user finishes a recast in the web app, export the contract they ALREADY get — but as a small JSON sidecar (.argus/contract.json) listing 3-6 falsifiable predicates extracted from existing data: the recast's human-required steps, blindspot's top risks, the governing_idea. (2) Add a PostToolUse/Stop hook (or a manual /argus-verdict skill) that, at session end in Claude Code, feeds the transcript + contract.json to one llm.ts call and emits a Verdict: which predicates held, which human-required step the agent actually touched, whether a flagged risk fired. (3) Run it on 10-15 real sessions (your own + a few dev users) and hand-check: does the Verdict agree with ground truth, and does the calibration number move in a way that would change the next plan? Kill criteria: if predicate-grading accuracy is <~70% against hand-labels, or if you cannot find target users who execute in an instrumentable runtime, the bet is dead — fall back to C's incremental Logbook and keep the manual outcome prompt. This proof touches zero production source (new skill files + one hook), reuses llm.ts/context-chain/blindspot wholesale, and directly tests the two load-bearing unknowns (can we observe? can we grade?) before committing to any chassis change.

concepts.name: ARGUS // The Judgment Engine (your decisions, modeled)
concepts.one_line: Stop shipping a flow that produces documents; ship a personal/team judgment model that drafts the decision FOR you in your own style on voyage 1, and gets measurably more right with every voyage until it can pre-answer most of what the flow used to ask.
concepts.thesis: The current shape is a local maximum because its center of gravity is the FLOW (ProgressiveFlow ~2670 lines + useProgressiveStore ~1786 lines), and the flow is stateless across voyages: every voyage starts from a blank LLM, re-asks generic questions, and the user re-teaches their preferences each time. The judgment model already exists in the codebase (judgment-vitality.ts ~760 lines builds per-stage fingerprints, gamma/rigidity scores, provenance, interventions; user-context.ts + navigator build a cross-voyage NavigatorProfile with overrideRate/dominantStrategy/tier; observation-engine.ts ~501 lines even does boss-calibration) — but it is a PASSENGER. The fingerprint is recorded as a signal and never read back; the user-context block is injected only into the boss/reviewer persona prompt (review-prompt.ts, boss-prompt.ts), NOT into buildInitialAnalysisPrompt / buildDeepeningPrompt (confirmed: progressive-prompts take only problemText+locale). C's "Mirror" accepts this passenger framing and makes it prettier — a read-only dashboard you LOOK at, deliberately "reference not directive" per CLAUDE.md. The radical bet: the model should be the PROTAGONIST and the ENGINE. The product's core noun becomes "your Judgment Model" — a versioned, inspectable, per-user (and per-team) artifact that (1) pre-drafts every stage of the next decision in your style, (2) only asks you the questions where your model is genuinely uncertain or where it predicts you'll override, and (3) closes the loop by scoring its own predictions against what you actually decided, so "smarter every use" is a literal, measurable convergence curve — not a vibe. The flow demotes from product to training-data-collection ritual. "Just ask ChatGPT" can never answer this because ChatGPT has no persistent, self-correcting model of YOUR judgment.
concepts.what_fundamentally_changes: Today Argus IS a decision-harness flow whose output is 4 markdown files (이타카) and whose model is an invisible side-effect. After this, Argus IS a living Judgment Model whose output is a continuously-improving prediction of how YOU would reframe/recast/rehearse a decision — and the markdown is just one render of the model's current state. The unit of value flips from "a voyage" (a one-time event) to "your model at version N" (a compounding asset with a visible accuracy curve). The first screen of a returning user is no longer a blank "what's your problem?" — it's "Here's my draft of how you'd handle this; correct me where I'm wrong," with the questions pruned to only the ones the model can't predict. The retention thesis stops being "come back to re-read your log" (empirically unvalidated, per blindspot) and becomes "come back because the model you trained is now worth more than starting cold, and it's measurably more accurate than last month." Argus becomes the only place your decision-making style is captured as a portable, self-correcting object you (or your team) own.
what_it_kills: The flow-as-product framing: ProgressiveFlow.tsx (~2670 lines) is demoted from 'the product' to a thin 'training & correction surface' — most of its 29-hook orchestration for asking generic questions in fixed order is killed, because question selection now comes from the model's uncertainty, not a hardcoded sequence (pickNextQuestionType becomes model-driven).

The 'every voyage starts cold' assumption: buildInitialAnalysisPrompt / buildDeepeningPrompt as pure (problemText, locale) functions are killed; they MUST take the user's JudgmentModel as a first-class input.

The judgment data as decoration: getUserObservations()'s comment 'UI 전용 — 프롬프트에는 사용하지 않음' is killed outright. The whole CLAUDE.md guidance 'Pattern data is reference only, not directive / user patterns are secondary' is the SINGLE biggest doctrinal thing this kills — here the model IS directive (it drafts), with content-judgment as the corrector, not the reverse.

C's 'Mirror' as a passive read-only dashboard (useMirrorStore, Mirror.tsx spec): replaced by an ACTIVE model you edit and that acts on your behalf. Reflection becomes a side-effect of using the engine, not a destination tab.
The orphaned static-markdown 이타카 as the terminal artifact: outputs become a RENDER of model state, not the deliverable itself. The 4-file export survives but is no longer 'the point'.
The one-way learning loop (blindspot P0): signals-collected-never-acted-on is the exact thing this kills.
what_it_salvages: src/lib/llm.ts (~789 lines, backoff + circuit breaker + multi-fallback JSON) — untouched; the engine that makes model-drafting reliable.

src/lib/judgment-vitality.ts (~760 lines: buildStageFingerprint, computeStageGamma/ProjectGamma, detectRigiditySignals, assessVitality, generateInterventions, buildProvenanceChain) — this IS the half-built judgment model; it gets PROMOTED from signal-emitter to the core read path. Already wired into eval-engine.ts.

src/lib/observation-engine.ts (~501 lines, incl. analyzeBossCalibration/applyExplicitCalibration) — the self-correction machinery; repurposed from 'calibrate the boss persona' to 'calibrate the user's own model against actual decisions'.
src/lib/user-context.ts + navigator (NavigatorProfile: sessionCount, overrideRate, dominantStrategy, tier, dqTrend) — the cross-voyage aggregate; becomes the model's top-level summary.

Phase 1 adaptive decompose + Phase 2 multi-lens recast with working eval engines, and the Axis Fingerprint / Sliding-Window adaptation already in context-builder.ts (lines ~84,299,314) — these become the model's 'draft generators'.
useJudgmentStore / useAccuracyStore / signal-recorder.ts — the persistence spine for the model's training records.
The Claude Code skills (reframe/recast/rehearse/blindspot) + plugin — repurposed as the model's API surface: a skill can now load YOUR judgment model and draft in your style from inside the terminal.
concepts.why_better_for_the_real_user: A non-developer strategist's actual job is making the SAME class of decision repeatedly (market entries, hiring calls, vendor picks, roadmap bets) under their own evolving taste. ChatGPT treats decision #20 exactly like decision #1 — it has zero memory of that this strategist always under-verifies feasibility, always reclaims the first two steps for humans, and distrusts AI-suggested timelines (all things the existing fingerprint/navigator code can already detect). The Judgment Engine opens decision #20 with a draft that already reflects those tendencies and ONLY asks the 2-3 things it can't predict — so the strategist's time-per-decision drops while quality compounds. Crucially it's honest: it shows its own hit-rate ('I correctly predicted 8/11 of your calls last voyage; here's where I was wrong and why') so trust is earned by measured accuracy, not theater. That measurable, self-correcting, personal-to-you convergence is something a stateless chatbot structurally cannot offer — and it's a far sharper answer to the blindspot 'why not just ChatGPT' P0 than C's prettier flow.
concepts.biggest_risk: Cold-start + over-fitting: with n<5 voyages the model has nothing real to draft from, so early users get a generic draft dressed up as 'personalized' — recreating the exact 'false intimacy / metaphor without substance' trust-erosion the blindspot run flagged (team-assembly animation). Worse, an aggressive, directive model that drafts in 'your style' risks ANCHORING the user (they rubber-stamp the model's draft, judgment atrophies instead of compounds — the opposite of the thesis), and it directly violates the CLAUDE.md 'patterns are reference-only, never directive' safety doctrine that was likely written to prevent exactly this. If the self-scoring accuracy curve doesn't actually trend up (plausibly judgment is too context-dependent to model from structural fingerprints alone), the entire 'smarter every use' promise is falsified in public, on a number the user can see.
concepts.cheapest_proof: No new UI. In ONE existing surface, do a 2-part wizard-of-oz: (1) Inject the already-built buildUserContextForReview/NavigatorProfile block into buildInitialAnalysisPrompt (today it's only in the boss prompt) and have it PRE-FILL the first reframe/recast draft instead of asking blank — for the ~handful of internal users who already have 5+ voyages of signal history. (2) Before showing each generated question, have the model predict the user's answer/override from their fingerprint, store the prediction silently, then compare to what they actually answer. After ~10 voyages across a few users, compute one number: prediction accuracy, and whether it rises with voyage count. If accuracy is meaningfully above a generic-baseline AND trends up, the compounding model is real and worth the chassis rework. If it's flat or no better than generic, the radical bet is dead and C's incremental Mirror (model-as-passenger) is correctly the safer local maximum — say so and stop. This reuses judgment-vitality.ts + observation-engine.ts wholesale and writes essentially zero throwaway code.

concepts.name: The Sharpening — one provocation, one screen, ten seconds
concepts.one_line: Argus becomes a single-screen "prompt sharpener": you paste what you're about to ask AI, and in one shot it shows you the ONE thing you're getting wrong — the real question hiding under your stated one — with a copyable upgraded prompt, no voyage, no phases, no ceremony.
concepts.thesis: The 5-stage voyage (reframe→recast→rehearse→refine→이타카, 4 markdown outputs, 2670-line ProgressiveFlow) is a local maximum built on a category error: it treats "deciding what to have AI do" as a multi-session strategic project, when the real moment of truth is the 10 seconds before a non-developer hits Enter on ChatGPT. Blindspot's own P0 said the metaphor "obscures rather than clarifies" and that the real product doesn't start until interaction 2-3; the first-timer judges you on a 30s spinner then static markdown and leaves. Incremental-C's answer was to make the ceremony more beautiful (Departure screen, guided interview, 20s spectacle) — which makes the front door more ornate while the core loop stays slow. The radical bet: the differentiated, defensible move Argus already owns — Phase 1 adaptive-decompose that detects when real_question diverges from surface_task — is worth MORE delivered as a 10-second reflex than as the opening act of a voyage. Strip everything else. Win on speed and a single sharp move at the exact instant the user is about to "just ask ChatGPT," because that instant is where you can actually intercept them. Ceremony loses to speed at the moment of interception.
concepts.what_fundamentally_changes: Today Argus IS a decision harness / workspace you enter, settle into, and voyage through — a destination app that competes with "doing a strategy project." The Sharpening makes Argus a reflex you fire — a single-input tool that competes with the Enter key. The unit of value shifts from "a completed voyage with 4 artifacts and a logbook" to "one paste → one diagnosis → one better prompt, in under 10 seconds." It stops being a place you go and becomes the thing you bounce your prompt off of on the way to wherever you were already going (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini). The product's identity moves from "think before you recast" (an aspiration that asks for time you don't want to give) to "I'll tell you the one thing you're missing before you ask" (a transaction so cheap there's no reason not to). Retention stops depending on a "Mirror" or logbook you must come back to, and starts depending on the prompt being measurably better — the artifact IS the upgraded prompt you paste forward, so the value is realized in the very next tool, every single time.
what_it_kills: The voyage metaphor and its vocabulary as load-bearing UX — 항로 재설정/선원 배치/리허설/항로 수정/이타카 demoted from product stages to, at most, internal labels. Blindspot P0: it 'obscures rather than clarifies.'

ProgressiveFlow.tsx (~2670 lines) and useProgressiveStore (~1786 lines) as the chassis — the entire multi-phase state machine, waypoints, phase transitions, scroll choreography. Replaced by a single stateless request/response screen.

concepts.why_better_for_the_real_user: The real user is a non-developer strategist whose stated competitor is 'just asking ChatGPT directly.' Against that competitor, a voyage LOSES on every axis the user actually cares about in the moment: it's slower, it demands commitment, and its payoff (the 'aha') is buried at interaction 2-3 behind a spinner — so the user, by blindspot's own finding, has 'no coherent answer to why not ChatGPT' at first use and churns. The Sharpening wins precisely where ChatGPT can't defend: ChatGPT eagerly answers whatever you ask, including the wrong question — it has no incentive and no reflex to tell you 'you're asking the wrong thing.' Argus's one differentiated capability is exactly that reflex. Delivered in 10 seconds, with a copyable upgraded prompt, it slots into the user's existing habit (I was going to paste into ChatGPT anyway — now I paste here first, it costs me 10s, and I paste a sharper version forward). It respects that this user does NOT want a thinking ceremony; they want to not look foolish / not waste a generation on a misframed ask. Speed-to-felt-value goes from ~30-90s-plus-second-interaction to <10s, which is the only thing that converts a skeptic. And retention becomes self-evident rather than hoped-for: every upgraded prompt that produces a visibly better AI answer is a proof point that re-earns the next paste — no Mirror, no logbook guilt-trip required.
concepts.biggest_risk: Commoditization / 'is one sharp move enough to be a product?' Two failure modes: (1) The diagnosis isn't reliably better than asking ChatGPT 'what am I missing in this prompt?' — if GPT-5/Claude can self-critique a prompt nearly as well in one turn, Argus's single move is a thin wrapper with no moat, and a 10-second tool has nowhere to hide a weak output (the voyage at least hid mediocrity behind volume and ceremony). The entire bet rests on Phase 1 decompose producing a sharper, more surprising real_question than a naive 'critique my prompt' call — that quality gap must be real and felt. (2) Abandoning the voyage may discard genuine depth-users who DID want the multi-stage rehearsal/persona simulation; collapsing to one screen could trade a defensible 'deep work' niche for a crowded 'prompt helper' category. Plus a strategic risk: this makes Argus look more like the existing Claude Code skills, raising 'why a separate web app at all?' — the honest answer (reach non-developers who'll never touch a CLI) must hold.
concepts.cheapest_proof: A blind A/B taste test, buildable in ~1 day on existing infra, that isolates the ONLY thing in question — output quality at the moment of interception. Take 20-30 real misframed prompts (harvest from the demo scenarios + a few Slack/Reddit 'help me prompt this' asks). For each, generate three things: (A) what ChatGPT answers to the raw prompt, (B) ChatGPT's own one-turn 'what's wrong with this prompt + rewrite it', and (C) Argus's Phase 1 decompose → real_question + upgraded prompt (call progressive-engine.ts directly via a throwaway script, no UI needed). Show non-developer testers B vs C side-by-side, blind, and ask one question: 'which one surfaced something you hadn't already thought of?' If C doesn't win clearly (say >65%), the radical shape is a thin wrapper and you should NOT abandon the voyage — ship C's incremental onboarding instead. If C wins decisively, you've proven the single move is strong enough to stand alone, and the cheap second step is to wire that exact call into the existing InteractiveDemo screen as a real one-input form — a 1-2 day spike, not a rewrite — before touching ProgressiveFlow at all.

concepts.name: The Judgment Room — where a team's disagreement becomes a measurable, resolvable artifact before anyone touches AI
concepts.one_line: Argus stops being a solo "think before you recast" tool and becomes the shared room a team enters when they DON'T yet agree on what to ask AI to do — each member judges the same reframed decision blind, the room reveals where they diverge, and convergence_score (now measuring people, not the AI) is the deliverable a lead ships upward.
concepts.thesis: Incremental-C bet the moat lives "in the solo strategist's accumulating eye" and explicitly rejected peer comparison and new tables. That is the local maximum: a single-player reflection tool's honest ceiling is "a nicer ChatGPT with a journal," and its retention thesis is the one thing every prior run flagged as empirically unvalidated. The radical inversion: the recurring REAL pain across the blindspot personas isn't "I can't think clearly alone" — it's stakeholder misalignment (the CFO who'll object, the boss who'll reframe it, the peer who sees a risk you don't). Solo Argus SIMULATES those stakeholders (rehearse/persona-feedback). The Judgment Room makes them REAL: the actual humans submit judgment, blind, on the actual decision. The bet is that "we genuinely don't agree and need to before we burn a sprint" is a sharper, more fundable, harder-for-ChatGPT-to-touch job than "help me think alone." Decisively, this isn't greenfield: Argus already SHIPPED a dead team substrate (useTeamStore, /teams page, team_review_inputs with blind visible:false + owner-gated revealInputs + RLS) that the main voyage never wires in — the multiplayer chassis is half-built and abandoned, and convergence_score already exists as a computed metric begging to be repointed from AI-framing-stability to human-agreement.
concepts.what_fundamentally_changes: Today Argus IS a single-player decision harness: one person types a problem, an LLM reframes it, simulated personas react, one person reads four markdown files alone. It fundamentally becomes a synchronous-or-async team alignment instrument: a shared decision (one reframed real_question) that N real teammates each judge independently and blind, after which the room reveals the disagreement map and drives it toward a number everyone can see. The unit of value shifts from "a document I generated" to "the moment our team stopped silently disagreeing." The primary metric shifts from a private DQ/override score to a shared convergence_score that has organizational meaning ("we went from 41% to 83% aligned, here's the 2 reefs that moved us"). Retention shifts from "I personally come back" (one fragile user) to "my team's decisions live here and new decisions get routed here" (a workspace with switching cost). The buyer shifts from a curious individual to a team lead / PM / chief-of-staff who needs a defensible record of HOW the team aligned — a B2B wedge. AI moves from protagonist to referee: the LLM's job is no longer to be smart, it's to surface where humans differ and propose the minimal reframing that reconciles them.
what_it_kills: The solo 'Mirror / 나의 항로 감각' retention thesis from incremental-C — singular 'my judgment patterns' (navigator.ts NavigatorStrip personal sparkline) is demoted; the moat is now the SHARED room's convergence history, not one person's accumulating eye.

Simulated personas as the PRIMARY rehearsal mechanism — PersonaFeedbackStep / auto-persona.ts / worker-personas.ts become the FALLBACK for solo or async-missing teammates, not the headline. When a real CFO is in the room you don't simulate the CFO. This guts the blindspot finding 'team avatars suggest collaboration; reality is a single LLM call' by making the team real.

The four orphaned single-reader markdown outputs as the terminal artifact (FinalCard 이타카 / project-brief.ts / agent-spec.ts). The terminal artifact becomes the Convergence Record: divergence map + what moved + agreed real_question + minority report. Markdown export survives as a leaf, not the point.
'Think before you recast' as a SOLO tagline — replaced by 'Align before you recast.' The voyage's lonely 이타카 landfall is reframed as a shared harbor the whole crew reaches.
The load-bearing assumption (across DEEP-PLAN and TARGET-STATE) that retention must be solo-and-quiet, and the reality that the shipped /teams page is a dead-end CRUD disconnected from any voyage.
what_it_salvages: src/lib/llm.ts (~789 lines: backoff + circuit breaker + multi-fallback JSON) — untouched; the referee LLM needs the same reliable engine.

Phase 1 adaptive decompose + Phase 2 multi-lens recast (progressive-engine.ts, progressive-prompts.ts, eval-engine.ts) — these produce the SINGLE shared object (real_question, hidden_assumptions, skeleton steps, classified risks) the room judges. Content intelligence becomes the ballot, not the answer.

src/stores/useTeamStore.ts + src/app/teams/page.tsx + the shipped team_members/team_invites/team_review_inputs Supabase tables with RLS — the dead substrate IS the room. team_review_inputs already has phase + target_type ('assumption'|'step'|'risk'|'direction') + input_type ('rating'|'concern'|'endorsement'|'alternative') + visible:false + owner-gated revealInputs(): a blind-ballot-then-reveal primitive already built and abandoned. The core loop is ~80% plumbed.

src/lib/progressive-convergence.ts (assessConvergence / assessConvergenceWithWorkers, wordOverlap + variance-reduction math) — REPURPOSED: same algorithms, new inputs. Today it measures AI real_question stability across rounds; repoint it to measure variance across team members' TeamReviewInput ratings/positions.

persona-feedback / debate-engine.ts / refinement loop — repurposed as auto-fill for absent voters and as the referee that drafts 'the minimal reframing reconciling the CFO's cost concern with Design's scope concern.'
slack-blocks.ts + useSlackStore.ts (already shipped) — the async channel: post 'Judgment Room open, cast your read,' collect blind, reveal in-thread. Another half-built asset that suddenly has a job.
concepts.why_better_for_the_real_user: The non-developer strategist's real competitor is 'just ask ChatGPT.' ChatGPT cannot hold a blind, attributed, multi-person judgment ballot on YOUR specific reframed decision and show your VP exactly where five teammates disagreed and what moved them — that's not an LLM capability, it's a coordination artifact with social proof. Solo Argus loses to ChatGPT because both end in 'a markdown plan one person reads.' The Judgment Room wins because its output is something the strategist literally cannot produce in ChatGPT and cannot produce in a meeting either: a meeting surfaces the loudest voice; a blind ballot surfaces the TRUE distribution, then a measurable path to alignment. For a strategist whose actual job is getting stakeholders to commit before spending money, 'here's our convergence record, we moved 41%→83% and here are the two reframes that did it' is a fundable, promotable, defensible deliverable. It also fixes the unvalidated retention problem structurally: you return not from personal discipline but because your team's pending decisions are routed here and your name is on the ballot.
concepts.biggest_risk: Cold-start / multiplayer chicken-and-egg: value only appears when 3+ real teammates actually show up and judge, but the current product (and its anon free-tier funnel, quota-config.ts) is built for instant solo gratification — a single user landing in an empty room sees LESS than solo Argus today. Worse, B2B teams already drown in alignment tooling (Miro, Loom async, FigJam, Slack threads), so 'open a Judgment Room' must beat 'just DM the three people' — a behavior-change bet, not a capability bet. If teams won't reliably convene blind, the convergence_score-as-product thesis collapses back into the simulated-persona experience incremental-C already has, minus the solo polish. Secondary risk: blind-then-reveal can feel like surveillance to coworkers, creating org-political friction that kills adoption.
concepts.cheapest_proof: Don't build sync rooms or new tables — exploit what already ships. Wire the orphaned team_review_inputs + revealInputs into ONE existing voyage surface: after a solo user finishes reframe, add a single 'Get 2 colleagues' read before you commit' button that emails an invite (useTeamStore.inviteMember already exists) to judge just the real_question + top 3 assumptions blind, then render a divergence strip using the existing convergence math repointed to their ratings. Ship to ~10 real teams, or run it manually (strategist forwards the reframe to 3 coworkers via the shipped Slack blocks; you collect blind reads and hand-compute variance). Kill-criterion: if fewer than ~30% of solo users who hit the button get even 2 colleagues to actually submit, OR if teams that DO converge don't say 'this beat our usual meeting,' the multiplayer thesis is dead and incremental-C's solo Mirror is the correct local maximum — keep it. One repointed function (assessConvergence) + one already-built invite path + zero new tables = a days-not-weeks test of the only assumption that matters: will real teammates show up and judge.

concepts.name: Harbormaster — Argus as the judgment layer that lives inside the agent
concepts.one_line: Kill the standalone webapp as the center of gravity and ship Argus as a Claude Code plugin that intercepts execution-bound prompts in the terminal where strategists already work with AI, turning reframe→recast→rehearse→refine into a gate the user passes through on the way to running something — with the .argus/ folder as a durable, git-trackable decision ledger.
concepts.thesis: The webapp is a local maximum because it forces the strategist to LEAVE the place they actually act (the agent/terminal/IDE chat) to go think in a separate browser tab, then carry the result back by hand. That context-switch is the whole reason their stated real competitor — "just ask ChatGPT directly" — wins: ChatGPT is where the doing happens, so the thinking happens there too. Argus-the-webapp loses every time the user is already mid-flow with an agent. The radical move is to stop competing for the user's attention and instead SIT ON THE PATH they're already walking: the moment they're about to have an AI build/decide/execute something, Argus interposes the harness right there, in-channel, and then hands the sharpened prompt directly to the execution agent. The skills already do this — and crucially they already persist a typed context chain (.argus/reframe.md → recast.md → rehearse.md → refine.md via the CONTEXT-CONTRACT YAML schema) plus a journal, personas, and config. The thing incremental-C spends an 'L'-effort core-flow re-skin trying to make visible in the browser (the gold provenance thread) is ALREADY a set of plaintext files you can cat, diff, and commit. Incrementalism is polishing the wrong surface.
concepts.what_fundamentally_changes: Argus stops being a 'place you go to think' (a destination web product with sessions, Zustand stores, Supabase sync, a logbook UI) and becomes 'a behavior that happens to your prompts wherever you already command AI' (a plugin/harness). The unit of value shifts from a rendered voyage in a browser to a committed .argus/ decision ledger sitting next to the code/doc the decision produced. Retention stops being 'did they reopen the webapp' and becomes 'is the harness installed and does it fire on the next execution-bound prompt' — distribution and habit, not a return visit. The product's identity becomes: the judgment layer that AI agents pass through before they execute, the way a linter sits before a commit.
what_it_kills: ProgressiveFlow.tsx (~2670 lines) — the mega-component chassis is deleted, not refactored; the linear-voyage UI is replaced by the agent's own turn-by-turn chat
useProgressiveStore (~1786 lines) and the Zustand session/store layer — session state becomes plaintext .argus/*.md files instead of in-browser stores + Supabase rows

The entire src/lib/llm.ts execution engine AS A RUNTIME (789 lines of backoff/circuit-breaker/multi-fallback-JSON) — in agent-native mode the HOST agent (Claude Code) makes the model calls, so Argus no longer runs its own LLM client at all on the user's primary path
Supabase as the system of record for voyages — the decision ledger is the user's own filesystem/git, not a hosted DB; Supabase survives only for the thin marketing site's waitlist if at all

The dual-mode webapp confusion (Progressive vs legacy 4-step, the ?step= params, HeroFlow team-assembly theater) that BLINDSPOT flagged as P0/P1 — all of it evaporates because there is no webapp flow to be confused by
The webapp's retention thesis (Logbook aside, NavigatorStrip, judgment-vitality dashboard cards) as the PRIMARY moat surface — repurposed into a /patterns skill reading .argus/journal.md

Incremental-C's onboarding ceremony, AnchoringMoment modals, dawn-harbour canvas, LogbookCard editorial design system — all browser-chrome that an agent-native product does not need and will not build
what_it_salvages: The CONTENT INTELLIGENCE prompt assets — Phase 1 adaptive decompose, Phase 2 multi-lens recast logic, risk-classification, persona-design, convergence — these are largely PROMPT ENGINEERING and already exist in two forms: TS (progressive-engine.ts, progressive-prompts.ts) and markdown skill references (.claude/skills/*/references/*.md). The markdown versions become the product; the TS versions become the spec that keeps them honest

The CONTEXT-CONTRACT.md typed YAML schema — this is the crown jewel for agent-native: it already defines reframe→recast→rehearse→refine handoffs as plaintext contracts. It IS the provenance chain, already persisted, already diffable
The .argus/ persistence convention already wired into every skill (journal.md, reframe.md, recast.md, refine.md, personas.json, config.json) — the durable decision ledger exists today
The 18-agent persona library in argus-plugin/agents/*.md (chief_strategist, devils-advocate, the named stakeholder personas) — these power /rehearse natively as subagents
The eval engines' RUBRICS (the criteria, not the runtime) — repurposed as self-check checklists the skill prompts apply, or as an optional CLI verifier

llm.ts's resilience PATTERNS as an OPTIONAL 'headless' mode: a thin `argus` CLI for users NOT in an agent (e.g., CI, Cursor, a raw script) can still call models directly using the salvaged engine — so the strong engine isn't thrown away, it's demoted from 'always-on chassis' to 'fallback adapter for non-agent hosts'
The marketing landing (src/app/page.tsx Act1Voyage narrative) — kept as a thin static install/demo page: 'Think before you recast' → one button → `claude plugin install argus`
concepts.why_better_for_the_real_user: The target user is a NON-developer strategist whose real competitor is 'just ask ChatGPT.' The webapp loses to that competitor on the only axis that matters: friction-at-the-moment-of-action. Agent-native wins because the harness fires exactly where and when they're about to act — they type '이 기능 만들어줘' or 'should we expand to Japan, draft the plan' to their agent, and Argus interposes 'wait, that's not the real question' BEFORE the agent burns a long execution on the wrong target. That is literally the tagline 'Think before you recast' made physically true instead of aspirational. The strategist never context-switches, never copies a prompt between tabs, never re-explains their situation to a second tool. And they get something ChatGPT structurally cannot give: a committed .argus/ ledger — a plaintext, git-trackable record of WHY this decision was made, which assumption was doubted, what the CFO-persona objected to — sitting right next to the artifact it produced. Three months later they (or a teammate) can `git blame` the decision. That durable, in-place reasoning genealogy is the moat the webapp keeps trying to render and the agent-native shape just... has, as files.
concepts.biggest_risk: Distribution and trigger reliability. (1) The addressable market collapses from 'anyone with a browser' to 'people who run Claude Code / a compatible agent CLI' — and the stated target user is a NON-developer strategist, the population LEAST likely to be living in a terminal. If they're in ChatGPT's web UI, not an agent, Argus-the-plugin literally cannot reach them. (2) Even for agent users, the value depends on the harness actually FIRING at the right moment — a skill only triggers if invoked or if the host's skill-routing recognizes the intent; a silent failure-to-trigger means the user 'just asks' and never knows Argus existed. (3) You inherit the host agent's model/quality variance — Argus no longer controls the LLM call (llm.ts demoted), so output quality depends on whoever's Claude Code is configured how, and the carefully-tuned eval/resilience guarantees get weaker. Honest verdict: this beats incremental-C ONLY for the developer-adjacent strategist already in an agent. For the pure non-dev strategist in a browser, it's strictly worse, and incremental-C's polished webapp is the right bet. The radical shape is a sharper product for a narrower, different user — not a universal upgrade. The most credible path is HYBRID: ship agent-native as the primary surface for the agent-resident user while keeping a thin webapp demo, and let the .argus/ ledger be the shared spine both render.
concepts.cheapest_proof: Instrument trigger-and-handoff on the EXISTING plugin, no new build: take 15-20 agent-resident strategists/PMs, have them install argus-plugin as-is, and measure two numbers over two weeks — (a) of their execution-bound prompts ('build X', 'draft the plan for Y'), what fraction did they route through /reframe or /argus BEFORE executing (the trigger-fire rate), and (b) how many came back to a committed .argus/ ledger to reuse or cite a past decision (the in-place-moat signal). If trigger-fire is high and they spontaneously keep the .argus/ files, the agent-native bet is alive and worth deleting ProgressiveFlow for. If they install it and still 'just ask' their agent directly because the harness never fires at the right moment, the radical shape is dead and you should fund incremental-C instead. This costs a few prompt tweaks to log invocations, zero webapp work, and decisively answers whether the user's habit lives in the agent or in the browser.

concept.name: Argus Live — the Decision Room (a standing, replayable reasoning session, not an export)
concept.one_line: Argus stops being a document factory and becomes a persistent, addressable, replayable Decision Room: every voyage is a living URL you reopen, re-run, fork, and watch decay — the deliverable is the session itself, kept alive, never "exported."
concept.thesis: The current shape's local maximum is the "export." Argus spends 2670 lines of ProgressiveFlow + a context chain + working eval engines to manufacture four markdown files — and the instant they're produced, the product's relationship to the user ends. Blindspot proved this: outputs are orphaned static markdown, the learning loop is one-way, and retention is empirically unvalidated. C's answer is to bolt a reflection TAB ("Mirror / Sense of the Route") onto the side of that same pipeline — it makes the ledger prettier but the artifact is still dead the moment it's made, and the user's reason to return is still "go read a dashboard about yourself." The radical bet: a decision is not an event that produces a document, it is a STATE that persists and degrades. The real reason a non-developer returns is not to admire a chart of their judgment — it is because a decision they made is still pending in reality, its assumptions are aging, the world moved, and the AI they were about to "recast" to has new capabilities. If the session is a living object with a URL, a heartbeat (assumption freshness), and a re-run button wired to the same llm.ts + Phase 1/2 engines, then "revisit" stops being a willpower act and becomes a notification: "3 of the assumptions behind your 'India market entry' decision are now 47 days old; one was contradicted by the outcome you logged. Re-rehearse?" The process becomes the product because the process never ends — it just goes quiet until reality pokes it.
concept.what_fundamentally_changes: Today Argus IS a single-shot decision harness that emits 4 documents and forgets you. It becomes a registry of standing decisions, each one a live, addressable reasoning session (/room/[id]) that you reopen mid-flight, where the four "outputs" are not files but VIEWS of the session's current state — regenerated on demand, always reflecting the latest assumptions. The unit of value shifts from "the document I produced" to "the decision I'm still responsible for." A voyage doesn't "complete at 이타카" — it goes into a STANDING state with a freshness heartbeat. Re-running is first-class, not backtracking: editing the real_question forks the room (cheap, versioned) instead of triggering a feared 30s full re-analysis (the P2 blindspot finding). The retention thesis flips from pull (user must remember to come admire their Mirror) to push (the room itself decays and pings you). And critically it closes the one-way loop the deep-plan flagged: because the room is alive, the outcome you log months later flows BACK into the room's own assumptions, marking them validated/contradicted in place — the same surface, not a separate accuracy store nobody opens.
what_it_kills: The 'export' mental model entirely — FinalCard.tsx's 'Copy Document' / 'download 4 markdown files' as the terminal act. Outputs are no longer files you take away; they are live render-on-demand views (lib/export.ts, agent-spec.ts, checklist.ts become VIEW SERIALIZERS of room state, invoked each visit, never the endpoint).

이타카/voyage-completion as a terminal state — the 'you have arrived, here is your document' moment. Replaced by a STANDING state with a heartbeat. The nautical 'arrival' metaphor dies; a decision is never 'arrived,' it's pending-in-reality.

The withLog checkbox + 'decision log as optional footnote' (FinalCard.tsx:76-83, the P1 blindspot finding) — the log isn't an optional appendix to a document, it's literally the spine of the room; there is nothing else to be a footnote to.

C's standalone 'Mirror / Sense of the Route' reflection TAB as a separate retention surface — folded INTO the room. You don't visit a dashboard about your judgment; your judgment history lives as the version graph of your actual standing decisions. The across-voyages ledger is emergent, not a built screen.
The fear-gated backtracking modal C/blindspot wanted to add ('this will re-analyze, est 30s') — re-running becomes the primary verb, versioned and cheap-feeling, so the warning is obsolete.

The dual-mode legacy 4-step flow (ReframeStep/RecastStep et al. as separate ?step= entry points) — a room has no 'steps you tab between,' it has a current state and a history; legacy mode has no place to live and gets deleted.
what_it_salvages: src/lib/llm.ts (~789 lines, backoff + circuit breaker + multi-fallback JSON) — UNTOUCHED and now MORE valuable: every room re-run, fork, and freshness-triggered re-rehearse hits it, so the robust engine finally earns its complexity instead of firing once per voyage.

Phase 1 adaptive decompose + Phase 2 multi-lens recast + the working eval engines — become the room's 'recompute' core. The exact same intelligence, but invoked repeatedly against an evolving state rather than once.

context-chain.ts (typed ReframeContext/RecastContext + mergeAssumptionsIntoKeyAssumptions with inheritance/provenance, verified real per deep-plan self-critique) — this IS the room's data model. The radical shape just demands it be PERSISTED with _source provenance and a per-assumption timestamp + status field (validated/contradicted/stale), which is exactly the Phase 0 work the deep-plan already sequenced as foundational. We're not inventing a new spine; we're giving the existing one a heartbeat.

Supabase + the localStorage-first/sync architecture (CLAUDE.md) — already built for persistence; rooms are just ProgressiveSession rows promoted to first-class addressable entities with a status + freshness column.
useAccuracyStore / outcome-rating plumbing C identified — reused as the WRITE-BACK channel: a logged outcome stamps the specific room assumption it validates/contradicts, in place.

The Claude Code skills + plugin (reframe/recast/rehearse/blindspot) — become room ACTIONS triggerable from CLI against a room id, making the standing-decision usable from where developers/power-users actually work.
concept.why_better_for_the_real_user: The non-developer strategist's honest problem isn't 'I need a nicely formatted strategy doc' (ChatGPT does that, and C's Mirror doesn't beat ChatGPT — it just journals). Their real problem is that they made a consequential call weeks ago, the world has shifted, and they have no idea which of their original assumptions still hold or whether the decision needs revisiting before they commit budget/headcount. 'Just ask ChatGPT' is structurally incapable of this: ChatGPT has no memory of the specific decision, no timestamped assumptions, no heartbeat, no 're-run the exact same rigorous rehearsal against what changed.' Argus Live owns the ONE thing ChatGPT can't: continuity of a specific decision over time. The win for a non-dev is concrete and emotional — they reopen /room/india-entry and see in plain language 'you assumed regulatory approval by Q2; that assumption is 47 days old and you logged that it slipped — 3 downstream steps depend on it. Re-rehearse?' That is a reason to return that requires zero discipline and zero love of dashboards, because the product reaches out when reality moves the ground under a decision they're still accountable for.
concept.biggest_risk: Decisions may not actually have a long enough 'live' tail to sustain push-retention — most casual non-dev users may make a call, ship it, and never care again, meaning the heartbeat pings into the void and feel like spam (the same empirically-unvalidated-retention trap, just relocated). Equally, 'freshness/decay' requires a credible signal that an assumption is stale — without the user logging outcomes or some external world-signal, decay is just a timer, and a timer-driven 'your assumption is 47 days old' ping is noise, not insight. The whole bet rests on assumptions being individually addressable, time-stamped, and outcome-linkable — which means the Phase 0 persisted-provenance-context-chain (the deep-plan's hardest 2-week foundation) is a HARD prerequisite, not optional; if that slips, the radical shape collapses back into 'a saved session with a re-run button.'
concept.cheapest_proof: Don't build rooms, decay, or notifications. Run a 2-week Wizard-of-Oz on existing users: take ~15 completed voyages already in Supabase, and 3-6 weeks after completion send each user ONE manual message naming a specific original assumption from their voyage and asking 'Is this still true? Does this decision need a fresh look?' with a single 'Re-open & re-rehearse' link that just reloads their old session into the current flow. Measure two numbers only: (1) reply/click-through rate vs. a control group pinged with C's 'come see your judgment patterns' Mirror framing, and (2) of those who re-open, how many actually re-run vs. bounce. If the decision-still-pending framing beats the self-reflection framing on return AND a non-trivial fraction re-run, the living-room thesis is alive and the Phase 0 investment is justified. If nobody cares that their old assumptions aged, kill the radical shape and ship C's incremental Mirror — it's cheaper and the honest winner.

votes.verdict:
THE STRONGEST OF THE RADICAL SHAPES ON THIS LENS, AND IT BEATS C ON THE QUESTION C COULDN'T ANSWER — but its feasibility rests entirely on one unbuilt foundation, and its retention thesis is one honest Wizard-of-Oz test away from collapse. Pursue the test, not the build.

Why it wins on user-value-vs-ChatGPT (5/5): This is the rare radical reshape that names something ChatGPT is STRUCTURALLY, not incidentally, incapable of. ChatGPT can out-write Argus's four markdown files today — that's why C's 'Mirror' tab is weak: a journal of your judgment patterns is just a nicer dashboard, and a non-dev does not return to admire a dashboard. The honest non-dev problem is not 'format my strategy' — it is 'I committed to India-entry six weeks ago, the world moved, and I don't know which of my original assumptions still hold before I spend budget.' ChatGPT cannot own that: no memory of the SPECIFIC decision, no timestamped assumptions, no heartbeat, no ability to re-run the exact same rigorous rehearsal against what changed. Continuity-of-a-specific-decision-over-time is a genuine category ChatGPT cannot enter without becoming Argus. That is the only one of the radical pitches where 'just ask ChatGPT' is not a shrug but an actual structural impossibility. On THIS lens it is a clear 5.

Why feasibility is only 3/5 (verified, not assumed): I checked the code. The good news first — the session scaffolding the concept needs is ALREADY built: ProgressiveSession rows are already persisted to localStorage AND Supabase (progressive_sessions table, cross-device merge in useProgressiveStore.ts ~line 446-487) and already carry created_at/updated_at. So '/room/[id] you reopen' and 'fork is a versioned row' are nearly free. llm.ts (789 lines, confirmed) and Phase 1/2 engines are genuinely reusable as the recompute core. BUT the entire emotional payload — 'this assumption is 47 days old; you logged it was contradicted' — requires per-ASSUMPTION addressability that does not exist. Today assumptions are {assumption, risk_if_false, verified:boolean} strings inside context blobs (context-chain.ts): no stable ID, no per-assumption timestamp, no status enum (validated/contradicted/stale). And the claimed 'write-back channel' is wrong on inspection: useAccuracyStore rates PERSONAS, not assumptions — it cannot stamp 'this outcome contradicts that assumption' without being rebuilt. So the concept's own admission is correct and load-bearing: the Phase-0 persisted, provenance-stamped, assumption-as-first-class-entity model is a HARD prerequisite, the deep-plan's hardest 2-week foundation. Without it the whole shape degrades to 'a saved session with a re-run button' — which is exactly C minus the polish. 3/5: cheaper than it looks at the session layer, far more expensive than it claims at the assumption layer.

Why philosophy fidelity is 4/5: This is the most interesting axis. The shape KILLS the nautical 'arrival at 이타카' metaphor and the export — a violent break from the surface DNA. Yet it is arguably MORE faithful to Argus's deepest stated mission ('Think before you recast' — rigor before AI execution) than C is. A decision you re-rehearse when reality shifts is MORE 'thinking before you recast' than a document you produced once and filed. It betrays the metaphor to honor the mission. Docked one point only because 'the deliverable is never finished' risks the opposite failure of the original — a non-dev sometimes genuinely IS done and wants a clean artifact to paste into a deck; killing 'export' entirely (rather than demoting it) over-rotates.

Why moat 4/5: continuity-of-a-specific-decision is a real data moat that compounds (every logged outcome, every aged assumption deepens the lock-in) and is hard for a general chatbot to copy without per-user per-decision state ChatGPT does not keep. Not a 5 only because the moat is thin until users actually accumulate standing decisions with logged outcomes — and that accumulation is the very thing the retention risk threatens.

Net judgment vs C: On real-user-value, this BEATS C, decisively, because it answers the question C dodges (why would a non-dev return without discipline?). C's honest answer is 'they won't, much.' This shape's answer — 'because the product pings them when reality moves a decision they're accountable for' — is a real answer. But it is an UNVALIDATED real answer, and the concept itself ships the correct, cheap falsification test. Verdict: do not build rooms. Run the Wizard-of-Oz first.
votes.strongest_element: The push-vs-pull retention inversion grafted onto a SPECIFIC, NAMED, TIMESTAMPED assumption — 'you assumed regulatory approval by Q2; that assumption is 47 days old and you logged it slipped; 3 downstream steps depend on it. Re-rehearse?' This single mechanic is worth grafting onto C wholesale even if the room shape loses, because it converts retention from a willpower act (go admire your Mirror) into a reality-driven interrupt, and it is the one thing in either pitch that ChatGPT structurally cannot do. C's Mirror tab + this assumption-freshness ping = a far stronger incremental product than C alone, at a fraction of the full-room cost.
votes.fatal_flaw: The retention thesis is relocated, not de-risked — and decay-by-timer is noise, not insight. The whole bet assumes consequential non-dev decisions have a long 'live tail' the user still cares about weeks later. Most casual users make a call, ship it, and never look back, so the heartbeat pings into the void and reads as spam — the SAME empirically-unvalidated-retention trap the concept claims to escape. Worse, the only honest staleness signal is the user logging an outcome or a real external world-signal; absent that, 'your assumption is 47 days old' is a mere timer, and a timer dressed as insight erodes trust fast. The flaw is sharpened by the feasibility finding: the assumption-level provenance model (no per-assumption timestamp/status, accuracy store rates personas not assumptions) is the deep-plan's hardest 2-week foundation AND a hard prerequisite — so you must spend the most expensive build BEFORE you can learn whether anyone cares that assumptions age. That ordering is backwards and fatal if shipped on faith. The concept's own cheapest_proof is the correct escape hatch: the 2-week Wizard-of-Oz (manually ping ~15 existing Supabase voyages with one named aged assumption + 're-open' link, measure click-through vs C's self-reflection framing AND re-run rate). If the decision-still-pending framing does not beat the Mirror framing, kill the radical shape and ship C — cheaper and the honest winner.

KeyAssumption {assumption, importance, certainty, if_wrong} and HiddenAssumption {assumption, risk_if_false, verified?, evaluation?} have NO id, NO timestamp, NO status (validated/contradicted/stale), NO _source provenance. And progressive_sessions stores the whole session as ONE opaque JSONB blob with only a row-level updated_at — there is no addressable, time-stamped, outcome-linkable assumption anywhere. Every load-bearing sentence ('3 assumptions are 47 days old', 'one was contradicted by the outcome you logged', write-back 'in place') requires this. The concept admits this is the hard 2-week Phase 0 — that admission is honest. Realistic foundation cost is 3-4 weeks, not 2, and it must precede everything. NET: this is NOT a 6-month rebuild — it's a ~4-week foundation + a room shell (/room/[id] reusing ProgressiveFlow's state) + a decay cron that reuses existing email rails. That is genuinely buildable on this stack in a quarter, and the cost claim is honest-to-optimistic rather than dishonest. It beats C on moat (C's Mirror is a journal ChatGPT-equivalent; continuity-of-a-specific-decision is the one thing ChatGPT structurally cannot do) but the biggest_risk the concept self-identifies (decay-without-a-real-world-signal is just a spam timer) is the actual kill condition, and the cheapest_proof (Wizard-of-Oz ping on 15 existing voyages, decision-pending framing vs Mirror framing) is the correct, near-zero-cost gate to run BEFORE the 4-week Phase 0. votes.strongest_element: The write-back loop closure: making a logged outcome stamp the SPECIFIC assumption it validates/contradicts, in place, on the same surface — instead of a separate accuracy store nobody opens (useAccuracyStore today is exactly that orphaned store). This single graft fixes the deep-plan's one-way-learning-loop finding regardless of whether rooms/decay/push ever ship. It only requires giving assumptions an id and a status field and routing the existing useAccuracyStore.addRating write to target an assumption id. That is a 1-2 day change that delivers the highest-leverage insight in the whole concept ('your judgment was wrong HERE, on THIS premise') and is worth doing even inside C's incremental Mirror.
votes.fatal_flaw: The entire product reaches out to the user via a DECAY signal, but the only decay source the architecture can actually produce on its own is a timer (assumption age). Real staleness — 'the world moved, regulatory approval slipped' — requires either the user logging an outcome (low-discipline non-devs, the exact users targeted, mostly won't) or an external world-signal the system has no source for. So the heartbeat degrades to 'your assumption is 47 days old' age-pings, which is noise, not insight, and trains users to ignore the notification — collapsing the push-retention thesis into the same unvalidated-retention trap, just relocated from pull to push. The per-assumption schema (the hard, real prerequisite) is necessary but NOT sufficient: without a credible non-timer decay source, the room is a saved session with a re-run button and a spam cron.
