concept.name: Argus Verdict — the harness that grades its own advice
concept.one_line: Stop shipping four markdown files and walking away; instead embed Argus AT the Claude Code / Cursor execution boundary so the same judgment engine that planned the work watches the work happen, scores its own pre-flight calls against what actually shipped, and turns "did the flagged risk materialize?" from a question the user types into a fact Argus observes.
concept.thesis: The current shape is a local maximum because it severs itself from the only event that can prove it was right: execution. ARGUS today is a decision harness that ends at the artifact — four orphaned markdown docs (Brief/Chain/Spec/Checklist via FinalCard + progressive-handoff) handed to a user who then leaves for Claude Code/Cursor and never comes back. Blindspot's headline ("what the code SAYS vs what PRODUCTION does") and its two P0s ("no execution instrumentation", "outputs don't drive retention") are not bugs to patch — they are the same wound: Argus has no feedback from reality, so its learning loop is structurally one-way (signal-recorder.ts collects, navigator.ts never acts) and its core promise ("think before you recast") can never be graded. C (incremental) feels this and reaches for it, but flinches: C's "did the flagged risk materialize?" is a MANUAL prompt the user types days later — self-report about a tool they already abandoned, the weakest possible signal, gated on a user who left. The radical bet: the judgment is only worth accumulating if it's CALIBRATED, and calibration is impossible without watching execution. So move Argus to where execution lives. ARGUS already ships skills (reframe/recast/rehearse/blindspot) + a plugin INTO Claude Code — the execution boundary is already half-occupied. Turn that beachhead into the product: a planning pass that emits not a doc but a live "decision contract" (the recast's AI-vs-human assignments + blindspot's flagged risks, as checkable predicates), then a thin runtime wrapper/hook that observes the actual session (which steps the agent did, which the human overrode, which flagged risk actually fired, whether the governing_idea survived contact) and posts a Verdict back. Argus stops being a doc generator beside execution and becomes the judgment layer wrapped around it — the only configuration in which "you get smarter every use" is true rather than aspirational, because every run produces a graded prediction, not a saved opinion.
concept.what_fundamentally_changes: Today Argus IS a pre-flight document generator: a beautiful standalone web voyage whose output is inert markdown and whose competitor ("just ask ChatGPT") wins because ChatGPT also produces text and is one tab closer to execution. After this, Argus IS a closed-loop judgment instrument that lives at the execution seam: it makes falsifiable pre-flight calls ("this step must be human-judged"; "the CFO-cost risk will surface here"; "the real question is X not Y"), then measures them against what the agent runtime actually did, and reports a Verdict + calibration score. The unit of value shifts from "a document I read once" to "a prediction that got graded" — which means the retention asset (C's Logbook / navigator judgment layer) becomes a TRACK RECORD ("your risk-flags hit 71%; you over-trust the AI on data steps") instead of a mood-board of unvalidated self-reflection. The competitor flips too: you cannot get a calibrated judgment track record from ChatGPT, because ChatGPT doesn't watch your execution and doesn't remember being wrong. Argus becomes the thing that sits between intention and execution and keeps score — a harness in the literal engineering sense (a test/observation rig), not the nautical metaphor sense.
what_it_kills: The four orphaned static-markdown outputs as the TERMINAL deliverable (FinalCard.tsx export, progressive-handoff): Brief/Chain/Spec/Checklist stop being the end of the product and become the serializable 'decision contract' that the runtime wrapper later reads back and grades — markdown survives as a wire format, dies as the point of the product.

The standalone web app as the PRIMARY surface and the voyage-completion ceremony as the climax: 이타카/'arrival at the document' is no longer the end state. The web app demotes to a planning console + Verdict dashboard; the climax moves to post-execution ('here is how your plan survived contact').

C's MANUAL self-report outcome prompt ('did the flagged risk actually materialize?' typed by the user later) — killed and replaced by an OBSERVED outcome from the runtime hook. The whole point is that this signal must be measured, not remembered.
The one-way learning loop: signal-recorder.ts collecting signals that navigator.ts never consumes. Either it now feeds calibration, or it's dead weight.

The pretense of 'an AI team watches with you' (the HeroFlow team-assembly animation blindspot flagged as theatrical) — replaced by a real, smaller claim: 'Argus watches your execution and tells you where your plan was wrong.'
The nautical metaphor as load-bearing UX (reframe→recast→rehearse→refine→이타카 as the product's spine). It can stay as flavor but it cannot carry an instrument whose value is a calibration number.
what_it_salvages: src/lib/llm.ts (~789 lines: backoff + circuit breaker + multi-fallback JSON) — kept whole; the runtime wrapper's 'compare plan vs actual' and 'classify what the agent did' are LLM calls that need exactly this resilience at the execution boundary where flakiness is higher.

Phase 1 adaptive decompose + Phase 2 multi-lens recast with their working eval engines — these BECOME the contract generator: the recast's AI-vs-human role assignments and the decompose's critical_path are precisely the falsifiable predicates the wrapper checks against the real session.

The Claude Code skills (reframe/recast/rehearse/blindspot) + the existing plugin — THE wedge. They already execute inside Claude Code. They get a sibling: an observe/verdict skill (or a hook on Stop/PostToolUse) that reads the contract and the transcript. This is the cheapest possible execution-boundary foothold on this stack.

context-chain.ts / context-builder.ts (typed reframe→recast→exec handoff) — repurposed as the schema for the decision contract; the typed provenance is what makes a predicate checkable rather than prose.

navigator.ts / getUserPatterns / judgment-vitality / signal-recorder.ts (the judgment layer C wanted to promote) — kept, but upgraded from 'visible self-reflection' to 'calibrated track record' once it's fed observed outcomes.
blindspot's risk-classification engine — its flagged risks become the highest-value predicates to grade ('did this risk fire?'), which is also the most differentiated thing ChatGPT cannot do.
concept.why_better_for_the_real_user: The real user is a NON-developer strategist deciding WHAT to have AI do, whose honest alternative is pasting the problem into ChatGPT. Against that, today's Argus loses on the merits: it's more friction (30-40s, a voyage, four docs) to produce text the user must still re-key into the actual AI tool — ChatGPT is closer to the action and also outputs text. The execution-bound shape gives the strategist the one thing ChatGPT structurally cannot: 'Last time you told the AI to handle the pricing analysis itself, you overrode it 40% of the way through and the cost-risk Argus flagged is exactly what tripped you. This time, hold that step.' That is judgment calibrated by the strategist's OWN history of being right and wrong about delegating to AI — the literal 'think before you recast' promise, finally falsifiable. ChatGPT cannot say it because ChatGPT does not watch what the strategist actually did next and does not keep score. It also fixes the non-developer's deepest fear — 'I don't know which parts of this I can trust the AI with' — with evidence instead of vibes: the AI-vs-human boundary stops being a one-time guess in a doc and becomes a position that gets graded and tuned to this person's demonstrated judgment.
concept.biggest_risk: Distribution and observability collapse the user base. The whole bet rests on Argus being able to OBSERVE real execution — which on this stack means the agent runtime is Claude Code (skills/hooks can read the session/transcript) or Cursor. But the stated target user is a NON-developer strategist, and non-developers overwhelmingly do NOT execute in Claude Code/Cursor — they execute in ChatGPT, a chat UI, or by hand, none of which expose an instrumentable boundary Argus can hook. So there's a brutal scissors: the users who give clean execution signal (developers in agent runtimes) are not the target persona, and the target persona executes where Argus is blind. If you weaken 'observe' to 'user self-reports outcome,' you have collapsed back into C's manual prompt and the radical bet evaporates. Secondary risk: even with a hook, mapping a messy real transcript to 'did predicate P hold?' is itself an LLM judgment that can be wrong, so a miscalibrated Verdict is worse than no verdict (it teaches the user the wrong lesson with false authority). Net honest verdict: as a REPLACEMENT for C this is probably WORSE for the stated non-developer persona because of the distribution scissors; it is BETTER only if you either (a) accept a pivot of the target user toward 'people who execute with AI agents,' or (b) ship it as an additive 'Pro/dev' loop on top of C's incremental web product rather than instead of it. The execution-bound harness is the right NORTH for the loop-closing problem, but it should ride on C's chassis, not bulldoze it.
concept.cheapest_proof: One week, no rewrite, ride the existing plugin. Build a single new Claude Code artifact: an 'argus-verdict' skill/hook pair. (1) When a user finishes a recast in the web app, export the contract they ALREADY get — but as a small JSON sidecar (.argus/contract.json) listing 3-6 falsifiable predicates extracted from existing data: the recast's human-required steps, blindspot's top risks, the governing_idea. (2) Add a PostToolUse/Stop hook (or a manual /argus-verdict skill) that, at session end in Claude Code, feeds the transcript + contract.json to one llm.ts call and emits a Verdict: which predicates held, which human-required step the agent actually touched, whether a flagged risk fired. (3) Run it on 10-15 real sessions (your own + a few dev users) and hand-check: does the Verdict agree with ground truth, and does the calibration number move in a way that would change the next plan? Kill criteria: if predicate-grading accuracy is <~70% against hand-labels, or if you cannot find target users who execute in an instrumentable runtime, the bet is dead — fall back to C's incremental Logbook and keep the manual outcome prompt. This proof touches zero production source (new skill files + one hook), reuses llm.ts/context-chain/blindspot wholesale, and directly tests the two load-bearing unknowns (can we observe? can we grade?) before committing to any chassis change.

A non-dev does not execute in Claude Code or Cursor. They execute in a chat box or by hand. There is NO instrumentable boundary to hook for this persona. The instant you weaken "observe" to "user self-reports the outcome," you have collapsed into exactly C's manual prompt and the entire radical bet — the one thing ChatGPT structurally cannot do (watch your execution and keep score) — evaporates, because now ChatGPT could do it too (you're just typing what happened). So the value-vs-ChatGPT score of 4 is real ONLY for a user who is NOT the target user. For the actual non-dev strategist, the structural-advantage-over-ChatGPT drops to ~2. The concept earns its high marks on philosophy_fidelity (5) and moat_durability (5) because a calibrated track record of YOUR delegation judgment is the single most durable thing ChatGPT cannot replicate — but it earns a brutal feasibility_on_stack (2) because the persona who could feed it clean signal lives where Argus can hook, and the persona Argus targets lives where Argus is blind. As a REPLACEMENT for C: worse for the stated user. concept.name: ARGUS // The Judgment Engine (your decisions, modeled)
concept.one_line: Stop shipping a flow that produces documents; ship a personal/team judgment model that drafts the decision FOR you in your own style on voyage 1, and gets measurably more right with every voyage until it can pre-answer most of what the flow used to ask.
concept.thesis: The current shape is a local maximum because its center of gravity is the FLOW (ProgressiveFlow ~2670 lines + useProgressiveStore ~1786 lines), and the flow is stateless across voyages: every voyage starts from a blank LLM, re-asks generic questions, and the user re-teaches their preferences each time. The judgment model already exists in the codebase (judgment-vitality.ts ~760 lines builds per-stage fingerprints, gamma/rigidity scores, provenance, interventions; user-context.ts + navigator build a cross-voyage NavigatorProfile with overrideRate/dominantStrategy/tier; observation-engine.ts ~501 lines even does boss-calibration) — but it is a PASSENGER. The fingerprint is recorded as a signal and never read back; the user-context block is injected only into the boss/reviewer persona prompt (review-prompt.ts, boss-prompt.ts), NOT into buildInitialAnalysisPrompt / buildDeepeningPrompt (confirmed: progressive-prompts take only problemText+locale). C's "Mirror" accepts this passenger framing and makes it prettier — a read-only dashboard you LOOK at, deliberately "reference not directive" per CLAUDE.md. The radical bet: the model should be the PROTAGONIST and the ENGINE. The product's core noun becomes "your Judgment Model" — a versioned, inspectable, per-user (and per-team) artifact that (1) pre-drafts every stage of the next decision in your style, (2) only asks you the questions where your model is genuinely uncertain or where it predicts you'll override, and (3) closes the loop by scoring its own predictions against what you actually decided, so "smarter every use" is a literal, measurable convergence curve — not a vibe. The flow demotes from product to training-data-collection ritual. "Just ask ChatGPT" can never answer this because ChatGPT has no persistent, self-correcting model of YOUR judgment.
concept.what_fundamentally_changes: Today Argus IS a decision-harness flow whose output is 4 markdown files (이타카) and whose model is an invisible side-effect. After this, Argus IS a living Judgment Model whose output is a continuously-improving prediction of how YOU would reframe/recast/rehearse a decision — and the markdown is just one render of the model's current state. The unit of value flips from "a voyage" (a one-time event) to "your model at version N" (a compounding asset with a visible accuracy curve). The first screen of a returning user is no longer a blank "what's your problem?" — it's "Here's my draft of how you'd handle this; correct me where I'm wrong," with the questions pruned to only the ones the model can't predict. The retention thesis stops being "come back to re-read your log" (empirically unvalidated, per blindspot) and becomes "come back because the model you trained is now worth more than starting cold, and it's measurably more accurate than last month." Argus becomes the only place your decision-making style is captured as a portable, self-correcting object you (or your team) own.
what_it_kills: The flow-as-product framing: ProgressiveFlow.tsx (~2670 lines) is demoted from 'the product' to a thin 'training & correction surface' — most of its 29-hook orchestration for asking generic questions in fixed order is killed, because question selection now comes from the model's uncertainty, not a hardcoded sequence (pickNextQuestionType becomes model-driven).

The 'every voyage starts cold' assumption: buildInitialAnalysisPrompt / buildDeepeningPrompt as pure (problemText, locale) functions are killed; they MUST take the user's JudgmentModel as a first-class input.

The judgment data as decoration: getUserObservations()'s comment 'UI 전용 — 프롬프트에는 사용하지 않음' is killed outright. The whole CLAUDE.md guidance 'Pattern data is reference only, not directive / user patterns are secondary' is the SINGLE biggest doctrinal thing this kills — here the model IS directive (it drafts), with content-judgment as the corrector, not the reverse.

C's 'Mirror' as a passive read-only dashboard (useMirrorStore, Mirror.tsx spec): replaced by an ACTIVE model you edit and that acts on your behalf. Reflection becomes a side-effect of using the engine, not a destination tab.
The orphaned static-markdown 이타카 as the terminal artifact: outputs become a RENDER of model state, not the deliverable itself. The 4-file export survives but is no longer 'the point'.
The one-way learning loop (blindspot P0): signals-collected-never-acted-on is the exact thing this kills.
what_it_salvages: src/lib/llm.ts (~789 lines, backoff + circuit breaker + multi-fallback JSON) — untouched; the engine that makes model-drafting reliable.

src/lib/judgment-vitality.ts (~760 lines: buildStageFingerprint, computeStageGamma/ProjectGamma, detectRigiditySignals, assessVitality, generateInterventions, buildProvenanceChain) — this IS the half-built judgment model; it gets PROMOTED from signal-emitter to the core read path. Already wired into eval-engine.ts.

src/lib/observation-engine.ts (~501 lines, incl. analyzeBossCalibration/applyExplicitCalibration) — the self-correction machinery; repurposed from 'calibrate the boss persona' to 'calibrate the user's own model against actual decisions'.
src/lib/user-context.ts + navigator (NavigatorProfile: sessionCount, overrideRate, dominantStrategy, tier, dqTrend) — the cross-voyage aggregate; becomes the model's top-level summary.

Phase 1 adaptive decompose + Phase 2 multi-lens recast with working eval engines, and the Axis Fingerprint / Sliding-Window adaptation already in context-builder.ts (lines ~84,299,314) — these become the model's 'draft generators'.
useJudgmentStore / useAccuracyStore / signal-recorder.ts — the persistence spine for the model's training records.
The Claude Code skills (reframe/recast/rehearse/blindspot) + plugin — repurposed as the model's API surface: a skill can now load YOUR judgment model and draft in your style from inside the terminal.
concept.why_better_for_the_real_user: A non-developer strategist's actual job is making the SAME class of decision repeatedly (market entries, hiring calls, vendor picks, roadmap bets) under their own evolving taste. ChatGPT treats decision #20 exactly like decision #1 — it has zero memory of that this strategist always under-verifies feasibility, always reclaims the first two steps for humans, and distrusts AI-suggested timelines (all things the existing fingerprint/navigator code can already detect). The Judgment Engine opens decision #20 with a draft that already reflects those tendencies and ONLY asks the 2-3 things it can't predict — so the strategist's time-per-decision drops while quality compounds. Crucially it's honest: it shows its own hit-rate ('I correctly predicted 8/11 of your calls last voyage; here's where I was wrong and why') so trust is earned by measured accuracy, not theater. That measurable, self-correcting, personal-to-you convergence is something a stateless chatbot structurally cannot offer — and it's a far sharper answer to the blindspot 'why not just ChatGPT' P0 than C's prettier flow.
concept.biggest_risk: Cold-start + over-fitting: with n<5 voyages the model has nothing real to draft from, so early users get a generic draft dressed up as 'personalized' — recreating the exact 'false intimacy / metaphor without substance' trust-erosion the blindspot run flagged (team-assembly animation). Worse, an aggressive, directive model that drafts in 'your style' risks ANCHORING the user (they rubber-stamp the model's draft, judgment atrophies instead of compounds — the opposite of the thesis), and it directly violates the CLAUDE.md 'patterns are reference-only, never directive' safety doctrine that was likely written to prevent exactly this. If the self-scoring accuracy curve doesn't actually trend up (plausibly judgment is too context-dependent to model from structural fingerprints alone), the entire 'smarter every use' promise is falsified in public, on a number the user can see.
concept.cheapest_proof: No new UI. In ONE existing surface, do a 2-part wizard-of-oz: (1) Inject the already-built buildUserContextForReview/NavigatorProfile block into buildInitialAnalysisPrompt (today it's only in the boss prompt) and have it PRE-FILL the first reframe/recast draft instead of asking blank — for the ~handful of internal users who already have 5+ voyages of signal history. (2) Before showing each generated question, have the model predict the user's answer/override from their fingerprint, store the prediction silently, then compare to what they actually answer. After ~10 voyages across a few users, compute one number: prediction accuracy, and whether it rises with voyage count. If accuracy is meaningfully above a generic-baseline AND trends up, the compounding model is real and worth the chassis rework. If it's flat or no better than generic, the radical bet is dead and C's incremental Mirror (model-as-passenger) is correctly the safer local maximum — say so and stop. This reuses judgment-vitality.ts + observation-engine.ts wholesale and writes essentially zero throwaway code.

Real strategic judgment is dominated by per-decision context (this specific market, this specific hire) that judgment-vitality.ts's stage-level gamma/rigidity fingerprints do NOT capture; they model HOW you decide structurally, not WHAT you'd conclude about a novel situation. So accuracy may plateau at 'slightly-better-than-generic' — high enough to feel real in a demo, too low to justify demoting the flow and inverting the safety doctrine. Compounding this is verified cold-start: with the handful of internal users who have 5+ voyages, n is tiny and the 'self-correcting curve' is statistically unreadable for months, while every new external user gets a generic draft costumed as 'personalized' — re-triggering the exact false-intimacy trust erosion blindspot flagged. The flaw is structural, not fixable by craft: if judgment is too context-dependent to model from fingerprints, no amount of engine reliability (llm.ts) or pretty UI saves it, and the pitch has, to its credit, already written its own death certificate for that case.

votes.concept: ARGUS // The Judgment Engine (your decisions, modeled)
votes.lens: mission-fidelity (fidelity to deepest intent: help a human structure judgment before costly AI execution — NOT fidelity to the voyage metaphor or current flow implementation)
votes.verdict:
VERIFIED AND STRONG, but its mission-fidelity is split-brained — it serves the mission's OUTCOME superbly while betraying the mission's METHOD, and that tension is the whole ballgame.

WHAT I CONFIRMED IN CODE (this concept is not bluffing): buildInitialAnalysisPrompt(problemText, locale) is genuinely pure — no user model input (progressive-prompts.ts:23). buildUserContextForReview/NavigatorProfile appear ONLY in review-prompt.ts + navigator.ts, never in progressive-prompts — the 'judgment-data-as-passenger' claim is literally true. CLAUDE.md:59-60 says verbatim 'Pattern data is reference only, not directive' and 'user patterns are secondary' — the exact doctrine the concept inverts. The salvage targets are all real exported functions (buildStageFingerprint, assessVitality, generateInterventions, analyzeBossCalibration, applyExplicitCalibration in judgment-vitality.ts/observation-engine.ts), and navigator.ts already computes overrideRate/dominantStrategy/dqTrend/tier. hit-rate.ts already computes per-domain hit-rates. So the 'cheapest proof' is honest: the prediction-scoring spine and the tendency-detection both already exist — this is a re-wiring, not a green-field build. Feasibility is the concept's strongest card after value.

MISSION-FIDELITY VERDICT (the assigned lens): The mission is 'help a human structure judgment before costly AI execution.' Score the two halves separately. OUTCOME fidelity is near-perfect (5): a self-correcting personal model that pre-drafts decision #20 from your real tendencies is the single most defensible answer to the 'why not just ChatGPT' P0 that any of the three workflows produced — ChatGPT is structurally stateless about YOU, and this is the only shape where 'smarter every use' becomes a literal number, not a vibe. That is a genuine moat (5) ChatGPT cannot copy without persistent per-user judgment state. But METHOD fidelity is where it bleeds (hence philosophy 3, not 5): the mission word is STRUCTURE judgment, not REPLACE judgment. A model that 'drafts the decision FOR you' and 'only asks the questions it can't predict' optimizes for time-per-decision and convergence — but the deepest intent of a decision harness sitting BEFORE execution is to make the human's OWN thinking sharper, so they catch the thing AI would have executed wrongly. The concept's own biggest_risk names this exactly (anchoring → judgment atrophy → rubber-stamping), and my read of CLAUDE.md:59-62 shows the 'reference-only, never directive' rule is a deliberately-written safety rail, not an accident of incrementalism. So this is the rare case where a shape can betray the metaphor (voyage→이타카 demoted to a render) AND be more faithful to the mission's outcome, while simultaneously threatening the mission's method. That is not a wash — it's the most interesting tension in the whole concept, and the concept is admirably honest that its own success metric (the public accuracy curve) is also its falsification condition.

WHERE IT BEATS C (incremental Mirror): decisively, on the one axis that matters most. C accepts the passenger framing and makes it prettier — a read-only Mirror you LOOK at. Blindspot already flagged C's retention thesis ('come back to re-read your log') as empirically unvalidated. This concept's retention thesis ('come back because your trained model is worth more than cold-start, and measurably more accurate than last month') is the first one across all four workflows that is both falsifiable AND structurally un-copyable. If the accuracy curve trends up, this is simply a better product than C. If it's flat, the concept tells you to kill itself and ship C — which is the correct, honest fallback.

NET: Worth the chassis rework ONLY conditional on the cheapest_proof passing, and ONLY if built as 'draft-as-scaffold-the-human-edits' rather than 'draft-the-human-approves.' The difference between those two implementations is the difference between serving the mission and betraying it — and the concept, as written, leans slightly toward the betraying one.
votes.strongest_element: The self-scoring convergence loop made PUBLIC and FALSIFIABLE: predict the user's answer/override from their existing fingerprint BEFORE asking, store it silently, then score against what they actually decided, and show the user the hit-rate ('I predicted 8/11 of your calls last voyage; here's where I was wrong'). This is graftable onto C or even today's flow with near-zero throwaway code because hit-rate.ts already computes hit-rates and navigator.ts already computes overrideRate — it closes the one-way learning loop (blindspot P0) and converts 'smarter every use' from marketing vibe into an auditable number. Even if the whole protagonist-model reshape loses, ship THIS as an instrument: it's the cheapest possible answer to blindspot's 'no execution instrumentation' and 'code-says vs production-does' headline, and trust earned by a visible number beats C's editorial polish.
votes.fatal_flaw: The accuracy curve is a double-edged sword that can falsify the product in public on a number the USER can see — and there are two independent ways it dies. (1) Empirical: judgment may be too context-dependent to predict from structural fingerprints alone (a market-entry call and a hiring call share overrideRate but almost nothing decision-relevant), so accuracy stays flat-or-near-generic-baseline and the entire 'compounding model' promise is falsified live. (2) Behavioral, and worse: even if accuracy DOES rise, it may rise because the directive draft ANCHORS the user into rubber-stamping — so the curve goes up while the human's actual judgment atrophies, inverting the mission (structure judgment → replace judgment) precisely as the CLAUDE.md 'reference-only, never directive' rail was written to prevent. The concept cannot distinguish these two from the accuracy number alone: a high hit-rate is consistent with both 'the model truly learned you' and 'the model trained you to agree with it.' Until the cheapest_proof also measures whether users OVERRIDE the draft at a healthy rate (anchoring guard) — not just whether the draft was accurate — the headline metric is unsafe to ship, because the success condition and the mission-betrayal condition produce the same green number.

concept.name: The Sharpening — one provocation, one screen, ten seconds
concept.one_line: Argus becomes a single-screen "prompt sharpener": you paste what you're about to ask AI, and in one shot it shows you the ONE thing you're getting wrong — the real question hiding under your stated one — with a copyable upgraded prompt, no voyage, no phases, no ceremony.
concept.thesis: The 5-stage voyage (reframe→recast→rehearse→refine→이타카, 4 markdown outputs, 2670-line ProgressiveFlow) is a local maximum built on a category error: it treats "deciding what to have AI do" as a multi-session strategic project, when the real moment of truth is the 10 seconds before a non-developer hits Enter on ChatGPT. Blindspot's own P0 said the metaphor "obscures rather than clarifies" and that the real product doesn't start until interaction 2-3; the first-timer judges you on a 30s spinner then static markdown and leaves. Incremental-C's answer was to make the ceremony more beautiful (Departure screen, guided interview, 20s spectacle) — which makes the front door more ornate while the core loop stays slow. The radical bet: the differentiated, defensible move Argus already owns — Phase 1 adaptive-decompose that detects when real_question diverges from surface_task — is worth MORE delivered as a 10-second reflex than as the opening act of a voyage. Strip everything else. Win on speed and a single sharp move at the exact instant the user is about to "just ask ChatGPT," because that instant is where you can actually intercept them. Ceremony loses to speed at the moment of interception.
concept.what_fundamentally_changes: Today Argus IS a decision harness / workspace you enter, settle into, and voyage through — a destination app that competes with "doing a strategy project." The Sharpening makes Argus a reflex you fire — a single-input tool that competes with the Enter key. The unit of value shifts from "a completed voyage with 4 artifacts and a logbook" to "one paste → one diagnosis → one better prompt, in under 10 seconds." It stops being a place you go and becomes the thing you bounce your prompt off of on the way to wherever you were already going (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini). The product's identity moves from "think before you recast" (an aspiration that asks for time you don't want to give) to "I'll tell you the one thing you're missing before you ask" (a transaction so cheap there's no reason not to). Retention stops depending on a "Mirror" or logbook you must come back to, and starts depending on the prompt being measurably better — the artifact IS the upgraded prompt you paste forward, so the value is realized in the very next tool, every single time.
what_it_kills: The voyage metaphor and its vocabulary as load-bearing UX — 항로 재설정/선원 배치/리허설/항로 수정/이타카 demoted from product stages to, at most, internal labels. Blindspot P0: it 'obscures rather than clarifies.'

ProgressiveFlow.tsx (~2670 lines) and useProgressiveStore (~1786 lines) as the chassis — the entire multi-phase state machine, waypoints, phase transitions, scroll choreography. Replaced by a single stateless request/response screen.
The 5-stage choreography and the conversational Q&A loop as the DEFAULT path — no more 30s initial-analysis spinner before the user sees value, no interaction-2 reveal.

The 4 orphaned markdown outputs (Project Brief / Prompt Chain / Agent Spec / Execution Checklist) as the deliverable — they were 'static, not living' (blindspot). Replaced by exactly one living artifact: the upgraded prompt itself.
The logbook / VoyageChart (three.js ~200KB) / branch-version-history UI as primary surface — kill the heavy chart, kill the branch tree as a first-class concept.

Incremental-C's entire onboarding apparatus — DepartureScreen ceremony, GuidedInterview Q1-Q4 gate, 20s Live Walkthrough auto-play. A 10-second tool needs no onboarding ceremony; the first use IS the onboarding.
The legacy 4-step flow (ReframeStep/RecastStep/RehearseStep) and the dual-flow confusion entirely — one screen, one path.
The persona/decision-maker/worker-deployment machinery as a required step — rehearsal becomes an optional, on-demand second click, not a stage.
what_it_salvages: src/lib/llm.ts (~789 lines: backoff + circuit breaker + multi-fallback JSON) — kept verbatim. The reliability engine is exactly what a one-shot tool needs to never hang; pair it with the deep-plan's P0 fix (60s stream timeout) and it's perfect for a reflex tool.

Phase 1 adaptive-decompose / progressive-engine.ts — this IS the product now. The real_question-vs-surface_task divergence detection becomes the single headline output. Repurposed from 'stage 1 of 5' to 'the whole thing.'

Phase 2 multi-lens recast + working eval engines — repurposed into the on-demand 'pressure-test' second action (one click: 'how would a skeptical reviewer attack this?'), not a mandatory rehearse stage.

InteractiveDemo.tsx + demo-data.ts — the scripted typing→analysis machine becomes the empty-state of the single screen (a pre-filled example that sharpens itself on load), giving instant show-don't-tell with near-zero new code. This is the one genuinely cheap idea to keep from C.

The Claude Code skills (reframe/recast/rehearse/blindspot) and the plugin — these are ALREADY the radical-simplification shipped correctly: one provocation, no ceremony. The web app should converge toward them, not diverge. They become the proof that the 10-second shape works.
The design tokens / 'dawn harbor' visual system (globals.css) — kept as skin, so the one screen still feels premium and editorial without needing the voyage scaffolding.
sanitize.ts / db.ts write-path safety and Supabase auth/quota — kept; a sharpener still needs rate limiting and optional save.
concept.why_better_for_the_real_user: The real user is a non-developer strategist whose stated competitor is 'just asking ChatGPT directly.' Against that competitor, a voyage LOSES on every axis the user actually cares about in the moment: it's slower, it demands commitment, and its payoff (the 'aha') is buried at interaction 2-3 behind a spinner — so the user, by blindspot's own finding, has 'no coherent answer to why not ChatGPT' at first use and churns. The Sharpening wins precisely where ChatGPT can't defend: ChatGPT eagerly answers whatever you ask, including the wrong question — it has no incentive and no reflex to tell you 'you're asking the wrong thing.' Argus's one differentiated capability is exactly that reflex. Delivered in 10 seconds, with a copyable upgraded prompt, it slots into the user's existing habit (I was going to paste into ChatGPT anyway — now I paste here first, it costs me 10s, and I paste a sharper version forward). It respects that this user does NOT want a thinking ceremony; they want to not look foolish / not waste a generation on a misframed ask. Speed-to-felt-value goes from ~30-90s-plus-second-interaction to <10s, which is the only thing that converts a skeptic. And retention becomes self-evident rather than hoped-for: every upgraded prompt that produces a visibly better AI answer is a proof point that re-earns the next paste — no Mirror, no logbook guilt-trip required.
concept.biggest_risk: Commoditization / 'is one sharp move enough to be a product?' Two failure modes: (1) The diagnosis isn't reliably better than asking ChatGPT 'what am I missing in this prompt?' — if GPT-5/Claude can self-critique a prompt nearly as well in one turn, Argus's single move is a thin wrapper with no moat, and a 10-second tool has nowhere to hide a weak output (the voyage at least hid mediocrity behind volume and ceremony). The entire bet rests on Phase 1 decompose producing a sharper, more surprising real_question than a naive 'critique my prompt' call — that quality gap must be real and felt. (2) Abandoning the voyage may discard genuine depth-users who DID want the multi-stage rehearsal/persona simulation; collapsing to one screen could trade a defensible 'deep work' niche for a crowded 'prompt helper' category. Plus a strategic risk: this makes Argus look more like the existing Claude Code skills, raising 'why a separate web app at all?' — the honest answer (reach non-developers who'll never touch a CLI) must hold.
concept.cheapest_proof: A blind A/B taste test, buildable in ~1 day on existing infra, that isolates the ONLY thing in question — output quality at the moment of interception. Take 20-30 real misframed prompts (harvest from the demo scenarios + a few Slack/Reddit 'help me prompt this' asks). For each, generate three things: (A) what ChatGPT answers to the raw prompt, (B) ChatGPT's own one-turn 'what's wrong with this prompt + rewrite it', and (C) Argus's Phase 1 decompose → real_question + upgraded prompt (call progressive-engine.ts directly via a throwaway script, no UI needed). Show non-developer testers B vs C side-by-side, blind, and ask one question: 'which one surfaced something you hadn't already thought of?' If C doesn't win clearly (say >65%), the radical shape is a thin wrapper and you should NOT abandon the voyage — ship C's incremental onboarding instead. If C wins decisively, you've proven the single move is strong enough to stand alone, and the cheap second step is to wire that exact call into the existing InteractiveDemo screen as a real one-input form — a 1-2 day spike, not a rewrite — before touching ProgressiveFlow at all.

votes.concept: The Sharpening — collapse Argus from a 5-stage voyage into a single-screen "prompt sharpener": paste your intended AI prompt, get back in <10s the one real_question hiding under your stated task plus a copyable upgraded prompt. Salvages llm.ts engine + Phase 1 decompose; kills ProgressiveFlow/useProgressiveStore chassis, the voyage metaphor, 4 markdown artifacts, logbook/three.js, and C's onboarding ceremony.
votes.lens: real-user-value (non-developer strategist whose rival is "just ask ChatGPT")
votes.verdict:
Through the real-user lens, this is the most honest concept of the radical set: it attacks the exact failure prior runs verified — value buried at interaction 2-3 behind a 30s spinner, so the first-timer has "no coherent answer to why not ChatGPT." Collapsing to one paste -> one diagnosis -> one copyable prompt aligns the unit of value with the user's actual moment of truth (the 10s before they hit Enter elsewhere), and it competes with the Enter key instead of with "doing a strategy project." That is a genuinely better fit for a user who explicitly does NOT want a ceremony. Feasibility is a 5: I verified llm.ts (789 lines) and progressive-engine.ts both exist and that real_question/hidden_assumptions are real first-class outputs (engine lines 309/387/460), and — crucially — a standalone /tools/reframe page already mounts ReframeStep, so the "single screen" is partly built; this is a wiring job, not a rewrite. The cheapest-proof (blind B-vs-C taste test isolating output quality) is exactly the right experiment and correctly self-falsifying.

But two things keep it from being a clear win over incremental-C through THIS lens. First, moat: the whole bet rests on Phase 1 decompose beating a naive "GPT-5, what am I missing in this prompt + rewrite it" call. With a frontier model the user already has open, that one-turn self-critique is increasingly good and free — a 10-second single-move tool has nowhere to hide a thin output, exactly as the concept admits. The differentiated reflex (AI won't tell you you're asking the wrong question) is real, but it's a prompt-engineering advantage, not a structural one, and it erodes as base models improve. Score 2 on moat is the honest read. Second, the concept overstates its own foundation: it claims "the Claude Code skills are already the radical-simplification shipped correctly: one provocation, no ceremony" — but reframe/SKILL.md actually does context-detection and AskUserQuestion gating (a mini Q&A), so the pure one-shot it idolizes doesn't fully exist yet even in the skills. That weakens the "we already proved the shape works" argument, though not fatally.

Net: as a STRATEGY ("intercept at the moment of interception, win on speed") this beats C for converting the skeptic. As a standalone PRODUCT it risks trading a defensible deep-work niche for the crowded prompt-helper category. The correct move is not "ship Sharpening instead of C" but "run the 1-day taste test first" — it gates both paths cheaply and is the single most valuable action in any of the four radical concepts. If C wins, the Sharpening becomes a fast front-door funnel INTO the voyage rather than a replacement, which is strictly better than either alone.
votes.strongest_element: The cheapest-proof: a 1-day blind B-vs-C taste test (ChatGPT's own one-turn "what's wrong + rewrite" vs Argus Phase 1 decompose, asking non-developers "which surfaced something you hadn't thought of?"). It isolates the ONE load-bearing uncertainty across this entire workflow — is Argus's signature move actually better than a free frontier self-critique — and is decisive either way. Worth running regardless of which concept wins, because every other radical and incremental bet silently assumes the answer is yes.
votes.fatal_flaw: Moat by erosion: the single move is a prompt-engineering edge over a self-critique the user can get for free from the frontier model they already have open. A 10-second one-shot tool gives output quality nowhere to hide, and as base models improve the gap the entire bet depends on narrows toward zero — leaving a thin wrapper in a crowded "prompt helper" category, which is a weaker position than the voyage's defensible (if slow) deep-work niche.

votes.concept: The Sharpening — one provocation, one screen, ten seconds
votes.verdict:
On the craft-and-feasibility lens this is the strongest of the radical shapes precisely because it is barely a rebuild — and I verified that on the source. The thing the whole bet rests on already exists as an isolated, callable function: progressive-engine.ts line 293 `runInitialAnalysis(...)` returns `{real_question, hidden_assumptions, skeleton}` in a single LLM round-trip (maxTokens 2000) with no dependency on useProgressiveStore. The reliability engine (llm.ts, 789 lines verified) and Phase 2 recast/eval are untouched. So "salvage the engine, kill the chassis" is not aspirational — the seam is real and clean. The kill list is genuinely deletable dead weight: ProgressiveFlow.tsx (2670 verified) + useProgressiveStore (1786 verified) are the chassis, not the value. The cheapest_proof is also honestly scoped: runInitialAnalysis is directly scriptable today with zero UI, so the blind A/B taste test is a ~1-day script, exactly as claimed. This is the rare radical concept where the cost estimate is not lying.

WHERE THE CRAFT CLAIM OVERREACHES (one correction): the concept says wiring the real call into InteractiveDemo.tsx is "near-zero new code" because the scripted typing machine is already there. I checked — InteractiveDemo.tsx (1852 lines) imports NEITHER progressive-engine NOR llm; it is a pure scripted animation over demo-data. So it gives you the *visual shell* for free, but the live-call path, streaming, the 60s timeout (deep-plan P0), error/empty/rate-limit states, and copy-forward UX are all net-new. Honest spike cost is 1-2 weeks for a shippable v1, not "1-2 days," though still nowhere near a 6-month rebuild. Feasibility stays a 5; the 1-day number applies only to the proof script, which is the right thing to do first.

The fatal weakness is NOT feasibility, it's moat (score 2), and the concept's own biggest_risk names it correctly. A 10-second one-shot tool has nowhere to hide a weak output, and its entire defensibility is the claim that Phase 1 decompose surfaces a sharper real_question than a frontier model's own "what am I missing in this prompt?" turn. That gap is unproven and, on a 2026 frontier model, plausibly thin — which is exactly why the cheapest_proof must run BEFORE any build, and why I trust the concept more for putting the kill-switch (>65% blind win or ship incremental-C instead) up front. As a buildable bet it is sound and cheap to falsify; as a durable product it is one prompt away from commoditization.
votes.strongest_element: The verified salvage seam: runInitialAnalysis (progressive-engine.ts:293) is already a store-free, single-round-trip function returning real_question + hidden_assumptions. Graft this regardless of the concept's fate — it means the differentiated "reframe" move can be exposed as a fast standalone endpoint/skill TODAY, decoupled from the 2670-line ProgressiveFlow, and reused by incremental-C as its onboarding "first aha" without waiting on the voyage. The proof script built on it costs a day and de-risks every other workflow's retention thesis.
votes.fatal_flaw: No moat at the one moment it claims to win. The product collapses to a single LLM call whose only defensible quality is "decompose beats naive self-critique" — an empirically unvalidated, easily-eroded gap against the very ChatGPT/Claude it intercepts. With ceremony stripped, there is zero margin to absorb a mediocre diagnosis, and the honest "why a separate web app vs. the existing skills" question (reach non-CLI users) is a distribution bet, not a product moat. If the blind A/B doesn't clear ~65%, there is nothing left to ship.

votes.concept: The Sharpening — one provocation, one screen, ten seconds (radical concept #4)
votes.lens: mission-fidelity (fidelity to the deepest intent: help a human structure judgment before costly AI execution — NOT fidelity to the voyage implementation)
votes.verdict:
STRONG SHAPE, FATAL MOAT — and the verification makes the verdict sharper than the concept itself claims. The deepest mission is "help a human structure judgment before costly AI execution." The Sharpening serves that mission MORE faithfully than the voyage does, because the voyage's central category error is real: it asks for a multi-session strategic commitment at a moment (the 10s before hitting Enter) when the user has already decided to spend zero minutes. A reflex that intercepts a misframed ask and hands back a sharper one IS "structuring judgment before costly execution" — just compressed to the only moment the target user will actually grant. So it betrays the voyage metaphor while honoring the mission. That is exactly the trade the judge lens is built to reward (hence philosophy_fidelity 4, not 2).

FEASIBILITY IS THE STRONGEST PART, AND UNDERSOLD. I verified runInitialAnalysis() in progressive-engine.ts (line 293) is already a standalone, streamable entry point taking ONLY problemText + an optional onToken callback, returning real_question + hidden_assumptions + skeleton — and buildInitialAnalysisPrompt(problemText, locale) is context-free (no Phase-0 pipeline, no store, no waypoint state required). The 2670-line ProgressiveFlow and 1786-line store sit ENTIRELY on top of this slice. The "one paste → one diagnosis" core is therefore not a rewrite; it is wiring one existing function into one new screen. The cheapest_proof (call the engine directly via a throwaway script) is literally true — no UI scaffolding needed to A/B the output. Feasibility is a clean 5.

WHERE I DOCK IT — MOAT (2), and it's the bet the whole thing rests on. The concept's own biggest_risk names this but underweights it. The single move — "tell you the real question under your stated one" — is precisely the move a frontier model self-critique ("what am I really asking here, rewrite my prompt") does competently in one turn, and that capability is improving on someone else's roadmap, not Argus's. A 10-second one-shot tool has, by design, nowhere to hide a thin output: strip the ceremony and the volume, and if the diagnosis is only marginally better than GPT-5's self-critique, there is no product. The voyage at least converted depth (multi-lens recast, persona rehearsal, eval engines — all genuinely strong, all verified salvageable) into felt value the raw model can't replicate in one shot. The Sharpening throws that differentiation overboard to win on speed at the moment of interception — but speed is not defensible (anyone can ship a fast textarea), and the one retained move is the LEAST defensible part of the engine. That is the inversion that worries me: it salvages the reliability chassis (llm.ts, correctly) but bets the company on the one capability most exposed to commoditization, while mothballing the capabilities (Phase 2 recast, eval, rehearsal) that are actually hard to clone.

USER VALUE (4). Against the user's OWN stated competitor ("just ask ChatGPT"), this wins where the voyage loses: it slots into the existing habit instead of replacing it, collapses speed-to-felt-value from ~30-90s+second-interaction to <10s, and gives a copyable artifact realized in the very next tool — no Mirror, no logbook guilt. That is a real, honest win on the conversion axis the prior runs flagged as fatal. It loses a point only because "is the one diagnosis reliably surprising?" is unproven, and the tool has no fallback if it isn't.

NET: This is the most mission-faithful AND most feasible of a radical reshape, and it correctly identifies that the voyage's front-door slowness is the actual churn driver. But as a STANDALONE product identity it is strictly more exposed than the incremental target C, because it discards the hard-to-clone depth and stakes everything on the one move frontier models are closing on. The right call is NOT either/or: run the cheapest_proof (1 day, real) AS THE GATE. The brilliance of this concept is not the product — it's that it proposes the exact experiment that should decide the roadmap. If C wins the blind taste test (>35% of the time GPT's self-critique matches Argus), the voyage's depth was load-bearing and you ship C's onboarding. If C wins decisively, you ship The Sharpening as the FRONT DOOR (fast reflex) and keep the voyage's depth as the optional second click — which is not a choice between the two concepts, it's the synthesis both runs were circling. Do not ship The Sharpening as a wholesale replacement; ship runInitialAnalysis as a 10-second front door that EARNS the right to offer the deeper engine. That keeps the moat (depth on demand) while fixing the interception problem (speed by default).
votes.strongest_element: The interception-moment reframe operationalized as a buildable spike: "the real product is the 10 seconds before Enter, and runInitialAnalysis() is already a context-free one-shot that delivers the differentiated real_question move." This is worth grafting into ANY future Argus regardless of whether the full concept wins — make the engine's first analysis the FRONT DOOR (instant, no ceremony, copyable upgraded prompt) and let it earn the right to invite the user deeper. It fixes the verified P0 (value buried behind a 30s spinner at interaction 2-3) at near-zero cost, and it's reversible: a fast front door over the existing engine costs almost nothing and doesn't require killing the voyage to test.
votes.fatal_flaw: The entire product collapses to a single move — "surface the real question under the stated one" — which is exactly the move a frontier model performs adequately in one self-critique turn, on a capability curve Argus does not control. A 10-second one-shot tool has no volume or ceremony to hide a thin output behind, so if Phase 1 decompose isn't decisively, repeatably MORE surprising than "GPT, rewrite my prompt" (the concept's own cheapest_proof bar: must win >65% blind), there is no defensible product — just a fast wrapper. And the concept makes this worse by jettisoning the genuinely hard-to-clone depth (multi-lens recast, eval engines, persona rehearsal — all verified strong and salvageable) in favor of betting everything on the single capability MOST exposed to commoditization. Speed wins the interception but cannot hold it; the moat had to come from the depth this shape throws away.

concept.name: The Judgment Room — where a team's disagreement becomes a measurable, resolvable artifact before anyone touches AI
concept.one_line: Argus stops being a solo "think before you recast" tool and becomes the shared room a team enters when they DON'T yet agree on what to ask AI to do — each member judges the same reframed decision blind, the room reveals where they diverge, and convergence_score (now measuring people, not the AI) is the deliverable a lead ships upward.
concept.thesis: Incremental-C bet the moat lives "in the solo strategist's accumulating eye" and explicitly rejected peer comparison and new tables. That is the local maximum: a single-player reflection tool's honest ceiling is "a nicer ChatGPT with a journal," and its retention thesis is the one thing every prior run flagged as empirically unvalidated. The radical inversion: the recurring REAL pain across the blindspot personas isn't "I can't think clearly alone" — it's stakeholder misalignment (the CFO who'll object, the boss who'll reframe it, the peer who sees a risk you don't). Solo Argus SIMULATES those stakeholders (rehearse/persona-feedback). The Judgment Room makes them REAL: the actual humans submit judgment, blind, on the actual decision. The bet is that "we genuinely don't agree and need to before we burn a sprint" is a sharper, more fundable, harder-for-ChatGPT-to-touch job than "help me think alone." Decisively, this isn't greenfield: Argus already SHIPPED a dead team substrate (useTeamStore, /teams page, team_review_inputs with blind visible:false + owner-gated revealInputs + RLS) that the main voyage never wires in — the multiplayer chassis is half-built and abandoned, and convergence_score already exists as a computed metric begging to be repointed from AI-framing-stability to human-agreement.
concept.what_fundamentally_changes: Today Argus IS a single-player decision harness: one person types a problem, an LLM reframes it, simulated personas react, one person reads four markdown files alone. It fundamentally becomes a synchronous-or-async team alignment instrument: a shared decision (one reframed real_question) that N real teammates each judge independently and blind, after which the room reveals the disagreement map and drives it toward a number everyone can see. The unit of value shifts from "a document I generated" to "the moment our team stopped silently disagreeing." The primary metric shifts from a private DQ/override score to a shared convergence_score that has organizational meaning ("we went from 41% to 83% aligned, here's the 2 reefs that moved us"). Retention shifts from "I personally come back" (one fragile user) to "my team's decisions live here and new decisions get routed here" (a workspace with switching cost). The buyer shifts from a curious individual to a team lead / PM / chief-of-staff who needs a defensible record of HOW the team aligned — a B2B wedge. AI moves from protagonist to referee: the LLM's job is no longer to be smart, it's to surface where humans differ and propose the minimal reframing that reconciles them.

concept.why_better_for_the_real_user: The non-developer strategist's real competitor is 'just ask ChatGPT.' ChatGPT cannot hold a blind, attributed, multi-person judgment ballot on YOUR specific reframed decision and show your VP exactly where five teammates disagreed and what moved them — that's not an LLM capability, it's a coordination artifact with social proof. Solo Argus loses to ChatGPT because both end in 'a markdown plan one person reads.' The Judgment Room wins because its output is something the strategist literally cannot produce in ChatGPT and cannot produce in a meeting either: a meeting surfaces the loudest voice; a blind ballot surfaces the TRUE distribution, then a measurable path to alignment. For a strategist whose actual job is getting stakeholders to commit before spending money, 'here's our convergence record, we moved 41%→83% and here are the two reframes that did it' is a fundable, promotable, defensible deliverable. It also fixes the unvalidated retention problem structurally: you return not from personal discipline but because your team's pending decisions are routed here and your name is on the ballot.
concept.biggest_risk: Cold-start / multiplayer chicken-and-egg: value only appears when 3+ real teammates actually show up and judge, but the current product (and its anon free-tier funnel, quota-config.ts) is built for instant solo gratification — a single user landing in an empty room sees LESS than solo Argus today. concept.cheapest_proof: Don't build sync rooms or new tables — exploit what already ships. Wire the orphaned team_review_inputs + revealInputs into ONE existing voyage surface: after a solo user finishes reframe, add a single 'Get 2 colleagues' read before you commit' button that emails an invite (useTeamStore.inviteMember already exists) to judge just the real_question + top 3 assumptions blind, then render a divergence strip using the existing convergence math repointed to their ratings. Kill-criterion: if fewer than ~30% of solo users who hit the button get even 2 colleagues to actually submit, OR if teams that DO converge don't say 'this beat our usual meeting,' the multiplayer thesis is dead and incremental-C's solo Mirror is the correct local maximum — keep it. One repointed function (assessConvergence) + one already-built invite path + zero new tables = a days-not-weeks test of the only assumption that matters: will real teammates show up and judge.

votes.lens: real-user-value (non-developer strategist whose rival is "just ask ChatGPT")
votes.verdict:
This is the single strongest of the radical departures on the real-user-value axis, and the only one that produces an artifact ChatGPT structurally cannot — but it wins by changing WHO the user is, which is both its power and its trap.

WHAT CHATGPT CANNOT DO (verified strong): The solo strategist loses to ChatGPT because both paths terminate in "a markdown plan one person reads." The Judgment Room's output — a blind, attributed, multi-person judgment distribution on YOUR specific reframed decision, plus a measurable path from 41%→83% with the two reframes that moved it — is genuinely outside an LLM's reach. It is a coordination artifact with social proof, not a generation. A meeting surfaces the loudest voice; a blind ballot surfaces the TRUE distribution. For a strategist whose actual job is getting the CFO/VP/peer to commit before a sprint burns, "here's our convergence record" is fundable, promotable, and defensible in a way no ChatGPT export ever is. On the stated rival, this scores a clean 5 — it's the only concept where ChatGPT is not even in the same category. The thesis that the real recurring pain is stakeholder MISALIGNMENT, not solo thinking, is the sharpest reframe any of the radical runs produced, and it correctly identifies that solo Argus already SIMULATES stakeholders (rehearse/persona-feedback) — making them real is a natural, not arbitrary, escalation.

FEASIBILITY IS UNUSUALLY HIGH FOR A RADICAL SHAPE (verified, score 4 not 5): I confirmed the substrate is real and abandoned. useTeamStore.ts ships submitReviewInput (forces visible:false server-side, strips client-controlled fields) + revealInputs (owner-gated, sets visible:true by project+phase) — a genuine blind-ballot-then-reveal primitive. TeamReviewInput in types.ts has exactly the claimed shape: phase, target_type ('assumption'|'step'|'risk'|'direction'), input_type ('rating'|'concern'|'endorsement'|'alternative'), visible. And grep proves the kill-claim: useTeamStore is imported in exactly TWO files — its own store and /teams/page.tsx, which imports ONLY the membership CRUD functions and never touches submitReviewInput/revealInputs/loadReviewInputs. The blind-ballot machinery is built, RLS-guarded, and wired to nothing. inviteMember exists. This is not greenfield. Docked one point because the concept oversells assessConvergence as "same algorithms, new inputs" — I read it: it computes wordOverlap between SEQUENTIAL real_question strings across rounds (longitudinal stability), not cross-sectional variance across N members' numeric ratings. Repointing it to people is NEW math (rating dispersion / position clustering), not a pure repoint. The convergence-score CONCEPT and UI scaffold transfer; the function body largely doesn't. Honest cost is "rewrite the metric, reuse the frame," not "repoint one function."

WHY ONLY 3 ON PHILOSOPHY: Argus's deepest intent is "judgment before execution — protect the human decision from premature AI recasting." The Judgment Room is FAITHFUL to that mission (it strengthens the before-AI gate) but BETRAYS the metaphor and the user. "Think before you recast" was explicitly, repeatedly a SOLO act of private discernment — the lonely voyage to 이타카. Converting it to "Align before you recast" doesn't extend the DNA, it swaps the protagonist: the curious individual strategist (the entire stated target user and the whole anon/solo funnel in quota-config) is demoted to "one voter," and the buyer becomes a PM/chief-of-staff. That may be a better BUSINESS, but it is a different product for a different person — which is the job of this lens to flag, not praise. It honors the mission while abandoning the user the mission was built for.

THE HONEST BOTTOM LINE vs INCREMENTAL-C: C bet the moat is "the solo strategist's accumulating eye" and every prior run flagged that retention thesis as empirically unvalidated. The Judgment Room is the more compelling answer to "what beats a nicer-ChatGPT-with-a-journal" — but it does NOT cleanly beat C for the user this lens cares about, because it only delivers value when 3+ real teammates show up. A single strategist landing in an empty room gets LESS than solo Argus today. So this isn't "radical beats incremental" — it's "a different, more fundable product sits next to incremental, gated behind a behavior-change bet C never had to make." The correct call is NOT to replace C with this. It is to run the cheapest-proof EXACTLY as written — it is genuinely days-not-weeks because the substrate is real — and let the kill-criterion decide: if <30% of solo users who hit a "get 2 colleagues' read" button get even 2 real submissions, the multiplayer thesis is dead and C's solo Mirror is the correct local maximum. This concept's greatest service is that it ships its own falsification test cheaply. Graft its wedge onto C as an experiment; do not bet the product on it yet.
votes.strongest_element: The "get 2 colleagues' blind read before you commit" button as a bolt-on to the EXISTING solo voyage — not a new product. After a solo user finishes reframe, one button emails an invite (inviteMember ships) to judge the real_question + top 3 assumptions blind via the already-built submitReviewInput/revealInputs primitive, then renders a divergence strip. This is graftable onto incremental-C with zero new tables, it converts solo Argus's single biggest weakness-vs-ChatGPT (output is a doc one person reads) into something ChatGPT cannot touch (an attributed blind distribution), and it is self-falsifying via a cheap conversion metric. Even if the full Judgment Room thesis loses, this one button is worth building because it tests the entire multiplayer bet for the cost of one screen.
votes.fatal_flaw: It silently swaps the user the product was built for. The whole stated target — the non-developer strategist whose rival is "just ask ChatGPT" — gets value here ONLY as a member of a convening team; a solo strategist in an empty room sees less than solo Argus delivers today. So the concept doesn't win the lens's user, it replaces them with a team lead, then inherits a behavior-change cold-start (must beat "just DM the 3 people" and out-convene Slack/FigJam/Loom) that is far harder than the capability bet C makes. For the individual this lens judges by, the radical shape is a downgrade until a critical mass of teammates reliably shows up blind — an assumption the product has zero evidence for and which the cheapest-proof exists precisely to kill.

votes.verdict: On craft-and-feasibility this is the strongest radical concept I can imagine for Argus, because its core claim is verifiable in the actual source and it is unusually honest about cost. I confirmed the load-bearing assertions: useTeamStore.ts genuinely ships a blind-ballot-then-reveal primitive — submitReviewInput hard-forces visible:false (line 254), revealInputs is owner-gated (line 265), inviteMember exists (line 123), all RLS-aware. team_review_inputs (types.ts L469-483) carries rating:number|null + target_type('assumption'|'step'|'risk'|'direction') + target_id — a schema PURPOSE-BUILT for per-target numeric ballots. And critically, I verified the substrate is DEAD: submitReviewInput/revealInputs/TeamReviewInput appear in only three files (the store, types, and teams/page.tsx) and NEVER in ProgressiveFlow.tsx or any voyage component. So the headline craft thesis — "a multiplayer chassis is half-built and abandoned, wire it into the voyage" — is true, not aspirational. The ASYNC core loop (invite → blind submit → owner reveal → render divergence) is genuinely ~80% plumbed and is a days-to-weeks job: one new ballot UI on an existing reframe surface, one new variance function, and re-using inviteMember + slack-blocks. Salvage of llm.ts / Phase1 / Phase2 / eval engines as "the ballot generator, not the answer" is clean and correct — those stay untouched. This is the rare radical reshape that does NOT need a 6-month rebuild. Two feasibility deductions keep it at 4 not 5. First, an honesty gap the concept glosses: it claims assessConvergence/wordOverlap is "REPURPOSED: same algorithms, new inputs." Not quite. The shipped function is a TIME-SERIES TEXT-stability metric (wordOverlap between consecutive real_question STRINGS across AI rounds, plus assumption-count trend). Inter-rater agreement on NUMERIC ratings grouped by target_id is a different computation (variance/std-dev across people on a fixed target). The "variance-reduction" idea transfers conceptually, but this is a NEW function, not a repoint — a small but real understatement. Second, the "synchronous room" framing is a true ground-up rebuild: nothing in the substrate is realtime (loadReviewInputs is a one-shot fetch; no Supabase Realtime subscriptions exist), so live presence/sync reveal is net-new. The concept's cheapest_proof wisely sidesteps this by shipping async-only — the correct and feasible call. Philosophy fidelity is the genuinely contested axis (3): this concept does not extend the voyage DNA, it INVERTS the protagonist (solo strategist → team), the metric's meaning (AI stability → human agreement), and the tagline (Think → Align before you recast). Whether that honors Argus's deepest intent ("judgment before execution") or betrays it ("the accumulating solo eye") is exactly the orthogonal bet this lens was asked to surface — it is defensible but it is a real departure, and it directly contradicts incremental-C's explicit rejection of peer comparison. On value-vs-ChatGPT it scores 5 honestly: a blind attributed multi-person ballot on YOUR specific reframed decision is categorically not an LLM capability, and it structurally fixes the unvalidated retention problem (you return because your name is on a pending ballot, not from personal discipline). Net: the cheapest_proof is the best-designed kill-test in any of the radical concepts — one repointed surface, one already-built invite path, zero new tables, a concrete <30% kill-criterion — and it tests the ONLY assumption that matters before spending real build. Recommend running that proof. It beats incremental-C on defensibility and feasibility-of-test; whether it beats it as a SHIPPED product hinges entirely on the cold-start bet, which the proof is correctly designed to settle cheaply.

Value only materializes when 3+ real teammates actually convene and judge blind, but every shipped funnel (anon free tier, quota-config, instant-solo voyage) optimizes for single-user gratification — a lone user landing in an empty room gets LESS than solo Argus today. The deeper craft problem the cheapest_proof can't fully de-risk: the substrate proves the BALLOT is buildable, but buildability was never the bottleneck — behavior change is. If teammates won't reliably show up and submit (the <30% kill-criterion), the whole thesis collapses back into the simulated-persona experience incremental-C already ships, minus the solo polish — meaning the radical departure would have spent its build budget to arrive at a strictly worse version of the local maximum it tried to escape.

votes.verdict:
This is the most mission-faithful of the radical shapes I can imagine for Argus, and its factual foundation is real — I verified every load-bearing claim. useTeamStore is imported by exactly ONE file (/teams/page.tsx, a CRUD dead-end) and never by the voyage. submitReviewInput and revealInputs — the blind-ballot-then-reveal primitives — have ZERO callers anywhere in src/. So the concept's spine — "a multiplayer chassis is half-built and abandoned, ~80% plumbed" — is accurate, not aspirational.

On the DEEPEST intent (structure judgment before costly AI execution), this scores higher than incremental-C, and that is the crux of the mission-fidelity lens. The mission was never "help one person journal." It was: do not let a human spend real money/effort having AI execute the WRONG framing. The single largest source of "wrong framing" in any organization is not solo fog — it is unsurfaced stakeholder disagreement that detonates AFTER execution starts. A blind ballot surfacing the TRUE distribution before a sprint burns is a purer expression of "think before you recast" than a prettier solo mirror. It also structurally cures the one wound every prior run flagged: the retention thesis was empirically unvalidated BECAUSE it rested on solo discipline; here retention is exogenous (your name is on a ballot your lead routed). And it lands the killing blow on the blindspot meta-critique — "team avatars suggest collaboration; reality is a single LLM call" — by making the humans real instead of simulated.

Note the metaphor/mission split the lens demands: this BETRAYS the voyage DNA. The lonely 이타카 landfall, the single-reader markdown outputs, the "accumulating eye" — all demoted. C was told to honor the metaphor; this honors the MISSION at the metaphor's expense, and I judge that trade correct. The voyage was always a UI poem wrapped around a judgment engine; the engine (llm.ts, Phase 1/2, eval-engine, convergence math) is what carries forward intact, and the concept salvages exactly those.

Why it does not score 5/5 on fidelity, and why I still rank it above C: the biggest_risk is honestly stated and real — cold-start. The mission is "help A human." The Judgment Room delivers near-zero value to one human in an empty room, and the entire current funnel (anon free-tier, quota-config, instant solo gratification) is built for that one human. So fidelity to the mission is conditional on convening 3+ people — a behavior-change bet competing with "just DM three coworkers" and a saturated alignment-tool market (FigJam/Miro/Loom/Slack). If teams don't reliably convene blind, the thesis collapses back INTO incremental-C's simulated-persona experience minus the solo polish — i.e., strictly worse. That conditionality is why philosophy_fidelity is 4 not 5: the deepest intent is served brilliantly for teams and abandoned for the solo user who is the product's current entire installed base and stated target ("non-developer strategist").

The decisive virtue is that the concept already knows this and prices it correctly. That is intellectually honest in exactly the way the mission-fidelity lens rewards: it treats "will real teammates show up and judge" as the ONLY assumption that matters and buys the answer in days, salvaging the engine either way.

Verdict: this is a fundable, ChatGPT-proof reshape that serves the deepest intent better than incremental-C FOR ITS TARGET (teams), is ~80% plumbed on the existing stack, and — critically — is non-destructive to fall back from. It does not strictly dominate C, because C wins the solo single-player case this concept weakens. The correct move is not to choose between them: run the cheapest_proof FIRST (days), because it cleanly adjudicates whether the solo local maximum is real. concept.name: Harbormaster — Argus as the judgment layer that lives inside the agent
concept.one_line: Kill the standalone webapp as the center of gravity and ship Argus as a Claude Code plugin that intercepts execution-bound prompts in the terminal where strategists already work with AI, turning reframe→recast→rehearse→refine into a gate the user passes through on the way to running something — with the .argus/ folder as a durable, git-trackable decision ledger.
concept.thesis: The webapp is a local maximum because it forces the strategist to LEAVE the place they actually act (the agent/terminal/IDE chat) to go think in a separate browser tab, then carry the result back by hand. Argus-the-webapp loses every time the user is already mid-flow with an agent. The radical move is to stop competing for the user's attention and instead SIT ON THE PATH they're already walking: the moment they're about to have an AI build/decide/execute something, Argus interposes the harness right there, in-channel, and then hands the sharpened prompt directly to the execution agent. The skills already do this — and crucially they already persist a typed context chain (.argus/reframe.md → recast.md → rehearse.md → refine.md via the CONTEXT-CONTRACT YAML schema) plus a journal, personas, and config.
